Misc. bug: GGUF loader accepts a tensor size that wraps to 0 after padding

### Name and Version

$ bin/llama-gguf --version
(inspection tool built from this repo; same ggml/gguf code path as llama-cli)

Tested commit: master 9558fa44 (also confirmed on branch gguf-pad-wrap-guard
with the fix). Debug build, AppleClang, Darwin arm64. The vulnerable code is
in ggml/src/gguf.cpp (gguf_init_from_reader) and is not tied to this commit;
it has been present for a long time.

### Operating systems

Mac, Other? (Please let us know in description)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library), Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell
# build the example tool
cmake -S . -B build -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build --target llama-gguf

# trigger: read a crafted GGUF with tensor-data checking enabled
bin/llama-gguf poc/pad_wrap.gguf r

# PoC generator (poc/gen_pad_wrap.py) builds poc/pad_wrap.gguf (384 bytes):
#   tensor a: F32, 64 elts, 256 bytes (valid)
#   tensor b: F32, ne = [4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1]
#            ggml_nbytes = 4 * 4 * (2^30 - 1) * (2^30 + 1) = 2^64 - 16
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

gguf_init_from_reader accumulates each tensor's padded size into ctx->size:

    size_t padded_size = GGML_PAD(ggml_nbytes(&ti.t), ctx->alignment);
    if (SIZE_MAX - ctx->size < padded_size) { /* reject */ }
    ctx->size += padded_size;

GGML_PAD rounds up: GGML_PAD(x, n) = ((x) + (n) - 1) & ~((n) - 1).
When ggml_nbytes is within (alignment - 1) of SIZE_MAX, the (x) + (n - 1)
addition wraps to a small value and the mask clears it to 0. With the default
alignment (32) and nbytes = 2^64 - 16:

    GGML_PAD(2^64 - 16, 32)
      = ((2^64 - 16) + 31) & ~31
      = (15) & ~31          // 64-bit overflow on the add
      = 0

So padded_size becomes 0, the SIZE_MAX guard (which checks padded_size, not
nbytes) always passes, and ctx->size only records tensor a's 256 bytes.
Tensor b still gets a ggml_tensor with ne = [4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1]
and a data pointer at the end of the 256-byte backing blob, but the context
no longer reflects its real size.

Downstream code that trusts the context size, or iterates a tensor by its
own dimensions, then reads out of bounds. examples/gguf hits this directly
(see logs): it accepts size = 18446744073709551600, reads b's data past the
backing blob, and aborts.

The wrap lands on exactly 0 for every power-of-two alignment (checked over
all 32 possible alignment values), so the window is reliably hit, not a
near-miss.

Suggested fix: reject before padding when nbytes + (alignment - 1) would
overflow. ctx->alignment is already validated as a non-zero power of two
earlier in the same function, so (alignment - 1) cannot underflow.

    const size_t nbytes = ggml_nbytes(&ti.t);
    if (nbytes > SIZE_MAX - (ctx->alignment - 1)) {
        GGML_LOG_ERROR("%s: tensor '%s' size %zu overflows after padding (alignment %zu)\n",
            __func__, ti.t.name, nbytes, ctx->alignment);
        gguf_free(ctx);
        return nullptr;
    }
    const size_t padded_size = GGML_PAD(nbytes, ctx->alignment);
    if (SIZE_MAX - ctx->size < padded_size) { /* reject */ }
    ctx->size += padded_size;

A test-gguf handcrafted case (TENSORS_NBYTES_PAD_WRAP, single F32 tensor with
the same ne) flips with this fix: master accepts (returns non-null), patched
rejects (returns null).

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression. The GGML_PAD-based accumulation in gguf_init_from_reader
has been there for a long time; no single commit introduced it.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

master 9558fa44 (bin/llama-gguf poc/pad_wrap.gguf r) -- accepts the wrapped
size, reads tensor b out of bounds, aborts:

```console
gguf_ex_read_1: tensor[1]: name = b, size = 18446744073709551600, offset = 256, type = f32, n_elts = 4611686018427387900
gguf_ex_read_1: reading tensor 1 data
gguf_ex_read_1: tensor[1]: n_dims = 3, ne = (4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1), name = b, data = 0x104c90270
b data[:10] : 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000
examples/gguf/gguf.cpp:269: GGML_ASSERT(gguf_ex_read_1(fname, check_data) && "failed to read gguf file") failed
```

b's data pointer (0x...270) is 256 bytes past a's (0x...170), i.e. one byte
after the 256-byte backing blob. data[0] reads out of bounds and returns
0.0; the check_data loop then aborts on the value mismatch. Exit 134.

Note: ASAN does not flag this over-read. ggml sub-allocates each tensor from
a larger arena, so the few bytes read past b stay inside one malloc region.
The assert message is the proof the read left b's own data. A harness that
walks b's full declared extent SEGVs about 15.7 KB past the arena.

With the fix (branch gguf-pad-wrap-guard), the same command rejects at the
parser before any tensor data is built:

```console
gguf_init_from_reader: tensor 'b' size 18446744073709551600 overflows after padding (alignment 32)
gguf_ex_read_0: failed to load 'poc/pad_wrap.gguf'
```

examples/gguf-hash on the same PoC: --xxh64 returns a bogus hash silently
(the 2^64 - 16 length wraps the internal input+len pointer, main loop is
skipped); --all (sha1/sha256) hangs walking the declared extent.

</details>

Misc. bug: windows: when the simple input reader reads EOF on stdin, all processes in the console are sent ctrl+c

### Name and Version

version: 0.5.0-dev (build 11254, commit 8019dc563)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-cli

### Command line

```shell
llama-cli.exe -m stories260K.gguf < nul > out.txt 2> err.txt
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When using the simple input reader under windows, when stdin reaches eof, the program calls GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_C_EVENT, 0); where the second argument being 0 means the signal is sent to all processes that share that console. Microsoft documents it as: "If this parameter is zero, the signal is generated in all processes that share the console of the calling process." (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/generateconsolectrlevent)
Many agent tools redirect stdin to null when invoking, which makes the program enter this branch and consider eof to have occurred; because agent tools pass the console directly on to the child process, this code directly kills the processes sharing the console with it (including the supervising process that called it).

Which reader is used is decided automatically: console::init() switches to the simple input reader when neither stdout nor stderr is a console (common/console.cpp:96-101), and only that reader contains this call. The other reader, used when stdout is a real console, has no such call anywhere in it.

The POSIX branch of the same function just returns false when it hits EOF, sending no event at all; the behaviour of the two platforms is asymmetric, so I think this broadcast was not designed on purpose.

To reproduce this problem, you can open a console window and start a long-running process in the window

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -Command "$i=0; while($true){ $i++; Write-Host alive $i; Start-Sleep 1 }"
```

then run the following in the same window

 ```powershell
llama-cli.exe -m stories260K.gguf < nul > out.txt 2> err.txt
```
If you want to reproduce it, you only need to make sure the simple input/output is being used: both output streams must leave the console, or use --simple-io to force this mode. If both output streams stay on the terminal (for example llama-cli.exe -m stories260K.gguf < nul), nothing is killed at all; what you see instead is the CLI spinning on the closed stdin.

I found this problem while calling the tool from inside a supervising process; the process was silently killed several times, with no error output at all. Any process sharing a console with llama-cli can be affected by this problem.

delete this call, and on EOF only return false. Nothing else needs to be added along the llama-completion chain; it already prints eof by user when it reads EOF and breaks out of the loop. But while deleting the broadcast, the other half has to be done: the main loop today directly continues when it gets empty input (tools/cli/cli-context.cpp:511), and the reason llama-cli < file can stop today depends precisely on the SIGINT that this broadcast emits; if it is not changed into a real exit condition it will just spin idle. Also, this cannot be solved by changing parameters: a second argument of 0 means all processes sharing that console, a non-zero one can only be a process group, and a process group is only addressable when it is started with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

While fuzzing llama.cpp, I found several uncaught integer overflows during tensor parsing.

First one is improper int-overflow guard at gguf_init_from_reader(). The existing validation attempts
to ensure that the total number of elements is representable:
```
if (ok && ggml_nelements(&info.t) > 0 &&
    ((INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[1] <= info.t.ne[0]) ||
     (INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[2] <= info.t.ne[0]*info.t.ne[1]) ||
     (INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[3] <= info.t.ne[0]*info.t.ne[1]*info.t.ne[2]))) {
    ...
}
```

However, the arithmetic performed by the validation itself can overflow in `ggml_nelements()`, before result is checked. Additionally,
if one of the elements is zero (or multiplication overflows to zero), the condition becomes false and validation skipped entirely.
 
Another one is missing guard for possible integer overflows in ggml_new_tensor_impl(), that cause many overflow errors in ggml.c.

Misc. bug: Ling 3.0 parser ignores response_format / json_schema

### Name and Version

version: 0.5.0-dev (build 11223, commit 4da633776)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
docker image ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:full-cuda-b11223, CUDA. The same code is in master at 31385c9ce.

### Operating systems

_No response_

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

_No response_

### Command line

```shell
llama-server --models-preset /presets.ini --models-max 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 -fa on -ngl 99 --jinja

# presets.ini
[Ling-3.0-flash]
model = /archive/Ling-3.0-flash-IQ3_XXS.gguf
dev = CUDA0
load-mode = none
ctx-size = 262144
cache-type-k = q8_0
cache-type-v = q8_0
spec-type = draft-mtp
spec-draft-n-max = 1
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With the dedicated Ling 3.0 parser (#28682), `response_format` is not enforced at all. Requests with `{"type":"json_schema", ...}` or `{"type":"json_object","schema":...}` get unconstrained output: markdown, JSON wrapped in ```` ```json ```` fences, enum values outside the schema. This happens with reasoning on and off.

Model: `bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF`, `Ling-3.0-flash-IQ3_XXS.gguf`, served by `llama-server --jinja` in router mode (`--models-preset`).

Control: on the same build and the same request, `gemma-4-26B-A4B` (QAT Q4_0) follows the schema in all 8 combinations (json_schema / json_object × reasoning on / off). So does `gemma-4-26B-A4B` on b10902.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "Ling-3.0-flash",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 800,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What color is the sky and how many legs does a cat have? Answer in markdown with an explanation."}],
  "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "r", "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"color": {"type": "string", "enum": ["RED", "BLUE"]}, "n": {"type": "integer"}},
    "required": ["color", "n"], "additionalProperties": false}}}
}'
```

Expected: `{"color": "BLUE", "n": 4}`.
Actual: a markdown answer with headings and prose. Removing `enable_thinking: false` gives the same result.

### Cause

`common/parsers/ling3.cpp` builds a grammar only for tool calls:

```cpp
auto include_grammar = has_tools && inputs.tool_choice != COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_NONE;
```

`inputs.json_schema` is never read. The `gemma4.cpp` and `qwen3-coder.cpp` parsers handle it:

```cpp
auto has_response_format = inputs.json_schema.is_object() && !inputs.json_schema.empty();
auto include_grammar     = has_response_format || (has_tools && inputs.tool_choice != COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_NONE);
...
if (has_response_format) {
    return generation_prompt + (reasoning << p.content(p.schema(p.json(), "response-format", inputs.json_schema)));
}
```

### Possible fix (sketch, untested)

Follow `qwen3-coder.cpp`:

1. Compute `has_response_format` and add it to `include_grammar`.
2. In the parser builder, before the tool branch: `if (has_response_format) return opener + reasoning + p.content(p.schema(p.json(), "response-format", inputs.json_schema)) + tail + end;`
3. When the grammar is built for a response format, make it non-lazy (`data.grammar_lazy = !has_response_format && inputs.tool_choice != COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_REQUIRED;`) and set the `CALL_START` trigger only when the grammar is lazy.

Tool calls work correctly with this parser; only structured output is affected.

webui: Use `toLocaleString()` format consistently across chat message statistics

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

llama.cpp's web UI currently sometimes uses locale formatting only for certain components like Total Tokens Generated and Generated Tokens. This issue proposes to consistently use this locale formatting across chat message statistics.

### Motivation

It is generally much easier to glance at values that use locale formatting than unformatted ones. This will also make llama.cpp's web UI format more consistent with the changes made in #18300 that were missed in PR's made after it.

### Possible Implementation

This would just require editing [tools/ui/src/lib/components/app/chat/ChatMessages/ChatMessageStatistics/ChatMessageStatistics.svelte](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c841aeeb8bb2fe417038dadfa9b007cf1a9ef950/tools/ui/src/lib/components/app/chat/ChatMessages/ChatMessageStatistics/ChatMessageStatistics.svelte) by adding `.toLocaleString()` at the end of variables that we want formatted.

We may also want to add locale formatting to stats currently printed using `.toFixed(2)`.  To format accordingly, we can either:

- Use in-line `options` parameter in `.toLocaleString(locale, options)` instead of the above (e.g. `.toLocalString(undefined, { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`)
- Use a common  number formatter (e.g. `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2})`)

I personally think that creating a common formatter might be the best way to do this, since it is commonly used across 3 separate variables.

Once we choose one of the two above methods for the `toFixed(2)` replacement, I can write a PR where I update:

- `tokensPerSecond`
- `agenticTimings!.toolCallsCount`
- `promptTokens`
- `agenticToolsPerSecond`

Eval bug: ggml-vulkan crash with vulkan 1.0

### Name and Version

I'm using ggml (from master, circa v0.25.3) in my own software.

ggml-vulcan requires Vulkan 1.2. To enforce this it calls (indirectly, via some templates) the vkEnumerateInstanceVersion function pointer from the Vulkan implementation and compares it to the constant for Vulkan 1.2.

Unfortunately,  vkEnumerateInstanceVersion was [only added at Vulkan 1.1](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/extensions.html#extendingvulkan-instanceanddeviceversions) and ggml-vulkan is calling it unconditionally.

I have a CL that add a quick null check before the call. If that function is null then it's Vulkan 1.0 and we can throw an exception, like we do if vkEnumerateInstanceVersion returns Vulkan 1.1.

query:
Misc. bug: /slots save/restore silently loses all prompt reuse on hybrid/recurrent models — checkpoints are never persisted

### Name and Version

```
version: 10068 (571d0d540)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

Verified still present on `master` (`178a6c44`): `tools/server/server-context.cpp`
has no commits between `571d0d540` and `178a6c44`.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.3, Apple M5 Pro, Metal)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```sh
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4_MOE.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 0 -ngl 99 --jinja \
  --slot-save-path ./kv
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=restore` reports complete success — `n_restored` equals
the full token count and the slot subsequently reports those tokens in
`/slots` — but the restored state is **never reused**. The next request with an
identical prefix reprocesses every token: `cache_n = 0`.

The endpoint therefore appears to work while delivering none of its benefit, and
says nothing about it at default verbosity.

On a hybrid/recurrent model this is not a partial regression, it is total: the
restore is worth exactly zero. Measured here on a 14,906-token prefix — restore
completes in 0.12s versus 75.9s to recompute, and then all 14,914 tokens are
recomputed anyway.

This is a **different bug** from the known in-memory checkpoint issues; see
"Relationship to existing issues" below. In-memory reuse on this setup is
healthy (97.9% hit rate) — only the on-disk path is broken.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Requires: a hybrid/recurrent model (e.g. Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6, DeltaNet, Mamba)
# and llama-server started with --slot-save-path
H='Content-Type: application/json'
U=http://127.0.0.1:8080

# a prompt long enough to be worth caching
P=$(python3 -c "print('### POLICY\n' + '\n'.join(f'Rule {i}: verify precondition {(i*7)%89} then record outcome {(i*13)%83}.' for i in range(300)))")

req() { jq -n --arg p "$1" '{prompt:$p, n_predict:1, cache_prompt:true}'; }

# 1. cold — populates a slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: a?
A:")" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}

# 2. find the slot that actually holds it, and save
ID=$(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r 'map(select(.n_prompt_tokens > 0))[0].id')
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=save" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_saved}'
#    → {"n_saved":5529}

# 3. wipe every slot
for i in $(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r '.[].id'); do curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$i?action=erase" >/dev/null; done

# 4. restore — reports full success
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=restore" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_restored}'
#    → {"n_restored":5529}

# 5. same prefix again, pinned to that slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: b?
A:" | jq --argjson s "$ID" '. + {id_slot:$s}')" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}   ← BUG: expected a large cache_n
```

Step 5 should reuse the prefix. It reprocesses all of it.

### What is actually happening

The prefix match itself is **correct**. `server-context.cpp:3149`

```cpp
n_past = slot.prompt.tokens.get_common_prefix(input_tokens);
```

returns the full 5,529 — restore does repopulate `slot.prompt.tokens`. The
result is then discarded a few lines later, at `server-context.cpp:3284-3318`:

```cpp
if (pos_min >= pos_min_thold) {
    const auto it = std::find_if(
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rbegin(),
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend(), ...);

    bool do_reset = it == slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend();     // :3300
    ...
    if (do_reset) {
        SLT_TRC(slot, "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data ...");
        pos_next = 0;
        n_past   = 0;                                          // :3317
    }
}
```

A hybrid/recurrent model cannot partially rewind its recurrent state, so a
context checkpoint is the only way to roll back to a prefix — a requirement
extended from SWA-only to hybrid/recurrent in #16382. After a restore,
`slot.prompt.checkpoints` is **empty**, so `do_reset` is always true.

It is empty for two compounding reasons:

1. **The save file never contained checkpoints.** `server-context.cpp:2529-2531`
   serializes only the token list and the sequence's KV cells:
   ```cpp
   const llama_tokens tokens = slot->prompt.tokens.get_text_tokens();
   const size_t nwrite = llama_state_seq_save_file(ctx_tgt, filepath.c_str(),
                                                   slot->id, tokens.data(), token_count);
   ```
2. **Restore then clears whatever was there.** `server-context.cpp:2576-2577`
   ```cpp
   slot->prompt.clear();              // clears tokens AND checkpoints
   slot->prompt.tokens.insert(tokens);
   ```

So the on-disk path can never satisfy the checkpoint requirement introduced by
#16382. `git log` shows the save/restore payload has not been touched
substantively since `1d36b3670` (2025-05-02); #16382 landed 2025-10-03.

Notably the **in-memory** prompt cache added in #16391 got this right — it
stores a whole `server_prompt`, checkpoints included
(`server-task.cpp`: `prompt = std::move(it_best->prompt);`), and even accounts
for checkpoint bytes in `server_prompt_cache_state::size()`. That is precisely
why RAM reuse works while disk reuse does not.

### Why this is invisible

The reset is logged with `SLT_TRC` → `LOG_TRC` → `LOG_LEVEL_TRACE` (= 4).
At default verbosity, and even at `-lv 3`, nothing is printed. Users see a
successful restore, a correct `n_restored`, correct `/slots` output, and silent
full reprocessing. `-lv 4` is required:

```
slot   operator(): id  3 | task 10 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to
lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, see
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
```

### Control experiment

To confirm checkpoints are the load-bearing mechanism rather than something
specific to restore — with **no save/restore involved at all**, only
`--ctx-checkpoints 0`:

```
1st (cold)  cache_n=0  prompt_n=5529
2nd (warm)  cache_n=0  prompt_n=5529   ← ordinary reuse also broken
```

Same log line, once. Two consecutive identical-prefix requests fail to reuse.
That is the same end state a restore leaves the slot in, reached by a different
route, and it confirms the causal chain.

### Ruled out

| hypothesis | test | result |
|---|---|---|
| wrong slot saved | saved the slot reporting `n_prompt_tokens > 0` | still `cache_n=0` |
| scheduler routed elsewhere | pinned `id_slot` | still `cache_n=0` |
| missing `n_keep` | `n_keep: -1` | still `cache_n=0` |
| unified KV | `--parallel 1 --no-kv-unified` (`kv_unified='false'`) | still `cache_n=0` |
| SWA truncation | model has no SWA keys; `qwen35moe.ssm.*` present | n/a |

(Incidentally: `--no-kv-unified` appears to be ignored while the slot count is
auto — `kv_unified` stays `'true'` until `--parallel` is given an explicit
value. Possibly worth its own issue.)

### Relationship to existing issues

- **#24055** (context checkpoints always invalidated on hybrid/recurrent) — open,
  in-memory only, no mention of `/slots` save/restore. **Not this bug**: our
  in-memory checkpoints work correctly (97.9% hit rate on the same model and
  build). This report is about checkpoints not surviving the *disk* round-trip.
- **#22384** (closed), **#20225**, **#19794** — all in-memory checkpoint
  matching/creation on hybrid models. Same subsystem, different failure.
- **#21831** — reports the same trace line, but for the in-memory path.
- **QwenLM/qwen-code#5760** proposes adopting `/slots` save/restore to eliminate
  re-prefill. Open and untriaged; it would not work today on these models.

### Possible fixes

1. **Sidecar file** (no libllama format change): in the save handler, write
   `filepath + ".ckpt"` containing each `common_prompt_checkpoint`'s
   `n_tokens`, `id_task`, `pos_min`, `pos_max` and the length-prefixed
   `data_tgt` / `data_dft` / `data_spec` blobs, behind a magic + version. In
   restore, rebuild `slot->prompt.checkpoints` after the `prompt.clear()` at
   :2576. A missing or version-mismatched sidecar degrades to today's behaviour.
2. **Unify the two paths**: serialize a whole `server_prompt_cache_state` so the
   on-disk format is a superset of the in-memory cache entry. Removes the
   divergence that produced this bug, at the cost of a larger change.

Either way, `ctx_dft` state is also not saved, so `--model-draft` setups will
desync after a restore.

**Caveat for implementers:** synthesizing a checkpoint at `pos_min = 0` in the
restore handler is *not* a valid shortcut. The matcher would take the
`cur.pos_min == 0` branch at :3298 and decode on top of a recurrent state that
has already consumed that token — silently corrupt output rather than merely
slow.

Reuse after a fix will be bounded by checkpoint granularity
(`--ctx-checkpoints`, `--checkpoint-min-step`), i.e. it should match in-memory
behaviour, not necessarily produce a full-prefix hit.

Eval bug: CUDA ROUND rounds half to even with an MSVC host compiler (test-backend-ops ROUND f16 fails)

### Name and Version

llama.cpp `84e76d8a2` (2026-09-24); the kernel is unchanged on `master` at `8212c7802` (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/unary.cu`,
`op_round` returns `round(x)`). Also seen on `e613ef2c8`.

### Operating systems

Windows 11 (x64)

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (compute capability 12.0), driver 616.92

### Build

CUDA 13.4 (`nvcc` 13.4.59), host compiler MSVC 19.51 (toolset 14.51.36231),
`-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`.

### Problem description

`test-backend-ops` fails the f16 ROUND cases on CUDA0; every f32 ROUND case passes:

```
ROUND(type=f16,ne_a=[128,2,2,2])     NMSE 3.2e-6 .. 5.3e-5 > 1e-7   FAIL
ROUND(type=f16,ne_a=[5,7,11,13])     FAIL
ROUND(type=f16,ne=[1024,1024,1,1])   FAIL
```

Cause, from the compiled code: in this build the device `round(float)` in `op_round` is lowered to
`cvt.rni.f32.f32` (SASS `FRND` with no rounding modifier), which rounds half to **even**. CUDA documents `roundf` as
rounding halfway cases away from zero (`include/crt/math_functions.h`, CUDA 13.4, lines 1600-1604), and the CPU
reference (UCRT `roundf`) does that, so every exact `.5` tie comes out one lower in magnitude than the reference.
Extracted from `unary.cu.obj`: `cvt.f32.f16 -> cvt.rni.f32.f32 -> cvt.rn.f16.f32`.

An exact error model over every f16 value in the test's input ranges (ties counted, each off by 1) predicts NMSE
3.59e-6 and 5.35e-5 for the two shapes, which matches the observed failures. f32 inputs in the test are random
floats, where an exact tie practically never occurs — hence only f16 fails.

### Proposed fix

Spell out round-half-away-from-zero so the result does not depend on how the host compiler's headers map `round`:

```cuda
static __device__ __forceinline__ float op_round(float x) {
    const float t = truncf(x);
    return fabsf(x - t) >= 0.5f ? t + copysignf(1.0f, x) : t;
}
```

`x - t` is exact (Sterbenz), and `|x| >= 2^23`, `±0`, `±inf` and NaN come back unchanged, as `roundf` returns them.
With this change the full `test-backend-ops` on CUDA0 passes on this machine (16449/16449), and ROUND passes 20/20
repeated runs.

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression that I can place: `op_round` has been `round(x)` since it was added.

### Impact

Small: in the model code `ggml_round` is only called from `src/models/granite-switch.cpp`. The test failure is what
shows it.

query:
Eval bug: llama-speculative changes the distribution at temp > 0

### Name and Version

Commit: `7fe450e19305b828c199d602c23a8337aaa1f03b`.

```console
version: 0.5.0-dev (build 11146, commit 7fe450e19)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

CPU build:

```sh
cmake -B build -DGGML_METAL=OFF -DGGML_BLAS=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target llama-speculative llama-server
```

### Operating systems

Mac, Linux

macOS 27.0; the existing Linux reproduction used Ubuntu 24.04 and gcc 13.3.

### GGML backends

CPU

### Hardware

Apple M1 Pro. The existing Linux results used Intel Xeon CPUs at 2.10 GHz and 2.80 GHz.

### Models

Tiny random Llama target and a noised copy as draft: F32, 2 layers, vocabulary size 8. Each GGUF is 24,064 bytes. The vocabulary is `a` through `h`, with EOS at `h` (id 7). The prompt `bcdbc` is ids `1,2,3,1,2`.

The self-contained archive below has both models and `repro_l3.py`.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-speculative` changes the output distribution at temperature greater than zero, even with `-np 1`.

On this fixture, after a first generated token of `f`, the next token is always `e`. The target's non-speculative distribution at that prefix gives `e` only about 0.345 probability, with the remaining mass on `g` and `h`.

Decode the archive below in the llama.cpp checkout, then run:

```sh
python3 repro_l3.py build/bin/llama-speculative target.gguf draft.gguf 1000
```

The script uses seeds 1 through 1000 and counts the token after a first generated `f`. It uses this command for each seed:

```sh
build/bin/llama-speculative -m target.gguf -md draft.gguf -p bcdbc -n 4 --spec-draft-n-max 3 \
  -c 64 -t 1 --cache-type-k f32 --cache-type-v f32 -fa off \
  --samplers 'penalties;top_k;top_p;min_p;temperature' -np 1 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-k 3 --top-p 1.0 --min-p 0.0 --repeat-penalty 1.0 --repeat-last-n 64 -s 11
```

The reference probabilities come from non-speculative `llama-server` with prompt `bcdbcf`, the same sampler settings, `n_probs=8`, and `post_sampling_probs=true`: `e=0.3454894722`, `g=0.4516915679`, `h=0.2028189600`.

Two parts of the example seem to explain the result:

- It samples the draft, sorts its candidates, then takes `cur_p->data[is].id`. With `-np 1`, that is the top candidate, rather than the sampled candidate stored in `selected`. Verification still uses the ratio test with the draft probability.
- On rejection, it sorts the target and draft candidates by token id and subtracts probabilities by array position. With top-k/top-p/min-p truncation, the two arrays can contain different token ids at the same position.

Both lines remain in source at `a3a1c4747fdc0dcad40b3946108b89375d9a7d0e`: [draft selection](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/a3a1c4747fdc0dcad40b3946108b89375d9a7d0e/examples/speculative/speculative.cpp#L570) and [residual subtraction](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/a3a1c4747fdc0dcad40b3946108b89375d9a7d0e/examples/speculative/speculative.cpp#L346). That is a source check; the runtime reproduction above is on the pinned build.

This report concerns `examples/speculative`, rather than the server paths changed by #27694.

Eval bug: EmbeddingGemma 2 with -fa on runs attention on the CPU unless the token count is a multiple of 256

### Name and Version

$ llama-server --version
version: 0.6.0-dev (build 1, commit a05e58c)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

NVIDIA RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell, 16 GB (sm_120)

### Models

[ggml-org/embeddinggemma-2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/embeddinggemma-2-GGUF), `embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With `-fa on`, EmbeddingGemma 2 is about 10x slower when the input length is not a multiple of 256 tokens. GPU utilization is 0% during those requests. With `-fa off`, the speed is the same at every length.

Server:

```sh
llama-server -m embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf --embedding -fa on -ngl 99 -fit off -c 4096 -b 4096 -ub 4096 -np 1
```

Repro (the first request is a warm-up):

```sh
URL=http://localhost:8080
TEXT=$(yes 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.' | head -n 500 | tr '\n' ' ')
TOKENS=$(curl -s $URL/tokenize -d "{\"content\": \"$TEXT\"}" | jq -c .tokens)
for n in 3840 3841 3840 3841; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$n tokens: %{time_total}s\n" $URL/embedding \
    -d "{\"content\": $(jq -c ".[:$n]" <<< "$TOKENS"), \"cache_prompt\": false}"
done
```

`cache_prompt: false` matters. With the prompt cache on, slot reuse hides the difference.

Results (seconds per request):

| tokens | -fa on | -fa off |
|-------:|-------:|--------:|
|   1024 |  0.054 |   0.056 |
|   1025 |  0.206 |   0.058 |
|   2048 |  0.080 |   0.111 |
|   2049 |  0.623 |   0.123 |
|   3840 |  0.17  |   0.30  |
|   3841 |  1.96  |   0.29  |

Likely cause: the full-attention layers of this model have head_dim 512. For D=512, the CUDA kernel selection requires `gqa_opt_applies`, which needs `K->ne[1] % FATTN_KQ_STRIDE == 0` (256):

- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/a05e58c981ea1ec863b2f5b11bbde66f7bb7aac6/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn.cu#L561
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/a05e58c981ea1ec863b2f5b11bbde66f7bb7aac6/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn.cu#L605-L611

Text generation pads the KV cache to 256, so it is not affected. An embedding batch is not padded, so `K->ne[1]` is the token count. When that is not a multiple of 256, no CUDA kernel is selected and FLASH_ATTN_EXT for those layers runs on the CPU.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown. Every build I tested is affected: b11457, b11505, b11562, b11563.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

The log does not show the fallback. Slot timings with `-fa on` (3840 tokens: 0.15 s, 3841 tokens: 1.90 s):

```console
0.29.793.255 I slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 16 | processing task, is_child = 0
0.29.939.436 I slot      release: id  0 | task 16 | stop processing: n_tokens = 3840, truncated = 0
0.29.965.744 I slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 18 | processing task, is_child = 0
0.31.866.773 I slot      release: id  0 | task 18 | stop processing: n_tokens = 3841, truncated = 0
```
</details>
hints:
Oh hey, I've been experiencing the same bug as well on a two different machines: my desktop with an RTX 5070 Ti, and my laptop with an RTX 2060. First noticed this with build b11514, seems to still be a problem as of b11574. Here's what Claude Opus 5.5 on the laptop had to say (don't have access to my desktop right now, sorry):

---

Reproduced on a different GPU (RTX 2060, sm_75), and there's a second symptom of the same cause: with the default `-fa auto`, Flash Attention is silently disabled for this model, so there's no CPU fallback but a much larger compute buffer.

**Setup:** build 11574 (`8bb3cf0d2`), CUDA 13.4, built from source with `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON`, RTX 2060 6 GB (driver 615.71.09). `embeddinggemma-2-BF16.gguf`, `--embeddings --pooling mean -np 1 -c 8192`.

| Flags | CUDA0 compute buffer | CUDA_Host compute buffer |
|---|---|---|
| `-fa auto -b 8192 -ub 8192` | 2112.19 MiB | 576.25 MiB |
| `-fa on -b 8192 -ub 8192` | 1088.19 MiB | 320.25 MiB |
| `-fa auto -b 512 -ub 512` | 54.01 MiB | 6.02 MiB |

With `-fa auto` the log says:
```
resolve_fused_ops: layer 5 is assigned to device CUDA0 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
```
The same two lines appear at `-ub 512`, so auto-detection fails regardless of batch size. The compute buffer is only large at `-ub 8192`, but a non-causal model needs `-ub` ≥ the longest input.

The cause seems to be the same as in the report above. `resolve_fused_ops` probes by reserving a graph of `n_tokens_per_seq * n_seqs` tokens, and `llm_fused_op_flash_attn_probe` sets `n_tokens_per_seq = 1`. For this model a 1-token K fails the D=512 `K->ne[1] % FATTN_KQ_STRIDE == 0` check, so the probe reports "not supported" even though a 256-multiple batch would work. The result is that `-fa auto` always resolves to off here.

The two modes force a bad choice:
- `-fa auto` (the default) is always off, with a ~2× larger compute buffer at `-ub 8192`.
- `-fa on` is half the memory, but the four global layers fall back to CPU unless the token count is a multiple of 256, as reported above.

_(Separately, there's a host-memory growth from `output_reserve` allocating a logits buffer for pooled embedding contexts, tracked in #29388 (fix PRs #30255, #30339). I'm seeing roughly 1 GiB of RSS per 1000 tokens on this model, but that's a different issue.)_

query:
Feature Request: avoid allocating logits buffer for encoder-only models

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

It is my understanding that `llama_context::output_reserve()` still fully allocates logits buffer for encoder-only models (BERT / XLM-RoBERTa: bge-m3, nomic-embed), which should never use those for their purpose. Local tests showing RAM memory growth compatible with `n_tokens` which leads me to believe it allocates the expected logits buffer by current logic (fix/design for #14204) 

```bash
=== bge-m3-f16.gguf
{"n_tokens":2000,"dim":1024}
n_vocab=250002  RSS before=796MiB after=2869MiB  growth=2074MiB
expected logits buffer n_vocab*N*4 = 1907MiB
=== nomic-embed-text-v1.5.f16.gguf
{"n_tokens":2000,"dim":768}
n_vocab=30522  RSS before=296MiB after=713MiB  growth=417MiB
expected logits buffer n_vocab*N*4 = 233MiB
```

My main hypothesis is that we really don't need that buffer in encoder-only models, so it would be nice to keep it free if that confirms.  

### Motivation

That memory is expensive (`(n_vocab * n_tokens * 4)` bytes) and from what I can see is RAM only, which makes it hard for smaller setups (homelab, consumer hardware).

### Possible Implementation

[#25964](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25964) would be relevant here as an opt-in `--no-logits-for-embeddings` flag potentially would apply here. However I think there's a simpler fix by just checking if the model has logits in the first place:
- At init: llama_context[ already builds a reserve graph](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-context.cpp#L676-L688) for prompt processing (`graph_reserve()`, then `get_gf_res_reserve()`. Right after that, record whether that graph has a logits output: `get_gf_res_reserve()->get_logits() != nullptr`.
- In [output_reserve():](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-context.cpp#L676-L688) use that recorded flag instead of has_logits = true. Keep the T5 special case as it is.
hints:
This also hits decoder-derived embedding models, and EmbeddingGemma is the worst case because of its 262,144-token vocabulary: the buffer costs exactly 1 MiB per token in the decode batch. `gemma-embedding` never builds a logits tensor (its graph only sets `res->t_embd`), so the whole allocation is unused, and `ggml_backend_buffer_clear(buf_output, 0)` touches every page, so it is resident anonymous memory rather than untouched virtual memory. The buffer only grows, so the peak stays for the life of the process.

Repro on `b10809` (linux-x64 release, also seen on linux-arm64), `ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-q8_0-GGUF`, one input per request, server restarted for each size:

```bash
llama-server -m embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf --embeddings -ub 2048 -b 2048 -c 2048 -np 1 -t 4 --port 38994
# then POST /v1/embeddings with {"input": "hello hello ... (N times)"}
# and read RssAnon from /proc/<pid>/status before and after
```

| prompt tokens | RssAnon growth (stock) | with the output buffer skipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 66 | 70 MiB | 4 MiB |
| 258 | 274 MiB | 15 MiB |
| 514 | 542 MiB | 27 MiB |
| 1026 | 1069 MiB | 41 MiB |
| 1538 | 1591 MiB | 54 MiB |
| 2002 | 2065 MiB | 61 MiB |

The right column is the same `b10809` source with a single test-only change in `llama_context::output_reserve()`, toggled by an environment variable so both columns come from one binary:

```cpp
bool has_logits = !(cparams.embeddings && getenv("REPRO_NO_LOGITS") != nullptr);
```

The returned 768-dim embedding for a 2048-byte markdown input was bit-identical with and without the buffer.

With the server's default 4 slots, inputs from different slots share one decode, so up to `n_ubatch` tokens land in the buffer at once. That is about 2.2 GB for EmbeddingGemma at `-ub 2048`, which is what got the embedder OOM-killed inside a 2.6 GB memory cgroup on small VPS hosts. `-np 1` is a workaround (it bounds the peak by the longest single input), but the per-token cost remains, so a fix along the lines proposed above (decide `has_logits` from whether the reserved graph has a logits tensor, keeping the T5 case) would also cover this architecture.

Same root cause hits decision models served via `/v1/systemone` (PR #29831). Clef-Flash (Qwen3.5-9B, n_vocab 248320), b11401 win-cuda-13.4, RTX 4080 16 GB, 32 GB RAM: decision mode needs the whole input in one ubatch, so `-b/-ub 32768`; then every request reserves ~1 MiB/token, e.g. `output_reserve: failed to allocate output buffer of size 5099.15 MiB` for a ~5k-token state → `Compute error`. An 800-token state works, ~1.6k+ fails with 3.6 GB free RAM, so the advertised long context is unusable locally. The decision head only reads span-pooled embeddings, logits are never used.

Data point from a Windows/CUDA deployment: Tesla P4 (8 GB) in a VM with 16 GB of RAM, serving `embeddinggemma-2` Q8_0 (`--embedding -c 8192 -b 8192 -ub 8192 -np 1`) and `bge-reranker-v2-m3` Q8_0 (`--reranking --pooling rank -c 16384 -b 1024 -ub 1024`).

I'm running b11476 (`9881906`) with the narrowest version of the fix:

```diff
-    bool has_logits     = true;
+    bool has_logits     = !cparams.embeddings;
```

That is only correct for contexts that never need logits. It holds for these two graphs (`gemma-embedding2` only sets `t_embd`; rank pooling reads the classifier output), and every access to the logits buffer is already guarded (`logits.data && t_logits` in decode/encode, `logits.size > 0` in `output_reorder`), so nothing else had to change. Deriving the flag from whether the reserve graph has a logits tensor, as proposed above, looks like the general version of this.

Process memory after the same workload, before → after:

| server | private bytes | working set |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| embeddinggemma-2 Q8_0 | 7,644 → 3,494 MB | 5,370 → 1,219 MB |
| bge-reranker-v2-m3 Q8_0 | 2,070 → 1,042 MB | 1,561 → 886 MB |

Outputs did not change: rerank scores identical over 617 query/document pairs (max abs diff 0.0, top-8 order identical in 25/25 queries), and embeddings identical against the same reference (192 documents; cosine to a bf16 sentence-transformers run on another GPU: mean 1.00035 / min 0.99804 with and without the change). Throughput did not drop.

Without it, `embeddinggemma-2` could not run next to `bge-m3` on this VM: with a full batch, `output_reserve` failed to allocate, requests returned HTTP 500 `Compute error`, followed by `CUDA error: out of memory`.

Comparison details, for transparency: "before" is the official `llama-b11476-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64` release for the embedding server, and an older local build (`d230ddd76`) for the reranker; "after" is b11476 built locally with this change plus an unrelated MMQ tile-size change for Q8_0 on Pascal, which does not touch host memory.

I’d like to take this up. Planning to open a small PR based on the original proposal: derive has_logits from whether the reserve graph actually produces a logits tensor in output_reserve() (will keep text to text transfr transformer as a special case intact).
This would cleanly handle models that never produce logits (EmbeddingGemma, BERT, rerankers) without breaking contexts that need both embeddings and completions.
I will test across a couple of embedding models and t5 and share before and after RSS numbers. @vschettino , please let me know if you already have a patch going; otherwise, I'll put up a pr shortly.

query:
Eval bug: qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) + MTP aborts on image input after #30257 (`GGML_ASSERT(ubatch.token …)` left in `graph_mtp`)

> **Disclosure:** This report was written by an AI assistant (Claude Code, Claude Sonnet 5.5) on behalf of a human, who asked for it and reviewed the text before posting. The reproduction and the patch test were run by the assistant on the human's machine.

### Name and Version

`llama-server` built from master `781dbc5ac` ("spec: properly handle mtmd input for mtp", #30257), tag `b11548`. Last good: `v0.6.0` (`d81235049`).

### Operating systems

Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV, AMD Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo iGPU, `-dev Vulkan1`)

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395), 128 GB unified memory, Vulkan RADV.

### Models

- Main: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next `UD-Q4_K_XL` (unsloth GGUF, 4 shards)
- MTP draft: `mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4_0.gguf` (ggml-org)
- mmproj: `mmproj-F16.gguf`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Starting the server with `--mmproj` and `--spec-type draft-mtp` and sending any request that contains an image makes the server abort in the MTP draft graph. Text-only requests are fine.

```
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf \
  -md mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4_0.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 \
  -dev Vulkan1 -c 262144 -np 1 -ngl 999 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 \
  --load-mode mmap --no-host --no-repack --fit off --port 8090
```

Request: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with one `image_url` (a 256x256 PNG, red/blue/green blocks, base64 data URI) plus the text "Welche Farben hat das Bild und wo?".

Result on master `781dbc5ac`: the process aborts, the client sees `RemoteDisconnected`:

```
src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:529: GGML_ASSERT(ubatch.token && "qwen4exp MTP requires token input") failed
...
#4  llama_model_qwen4exp::graph_mtp::graph_mtp(llama_model const&, llm_graph_params const&)
#5  llama_model_qwen4exp::build_arch_graph(llm_graph_params const&) const
#6  llama_model::build_graph(llm_graph_params const&) const
#7  llama_context::process_ubatch(...)
#8  llama_context::decode(llama_batch_ext const&)
#9  common_speculative_impl_draft_mtp::process(common_batch const&)
#10 common_speculative_process(common_speculative*, common_batch const&)
#11 process_mtmd_chunk(server_slot const&, ...)
#12 mtmd_helper_decode_image_chunk
```

The same request works on `v0.6.0`.

### Analysis

#30257 adds an embedding fallback to `llama_model_qwen4exp::graph_mtp`:

```cpp
ggml_tensor * tok_embd;
if (ubatch.token) {
    tok_embd = ggml_get_rows(ctx0, model.tok_embd, inp->tokens);
} else {
    tok_embd = inp->embd;
}
```

but the assertion a few lines above in the same constructor was not removed:

```cpp
GGML_ASSERT(ubatch.token && "qwen4exp MTP requires token input");   // src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:529
```

so the new `else` branch is unreachable and image chunks abort. (#30257 was tested with Qwen3.5-4B-MTP according to its description, which presumably does not have this assert.)

### Verification of the proposed fix

Deleting only that assertion line (patch attached) on top of `781dbc5ac`:

- the same image request succeeds; both repeats answer correctly (red top-left, blue top-right, green bottom), ~31-34 tok/s with MTP active
- the server keeps running; text requests afterwards behave as before (draft acceptance ~0.78 on a code prompt, ~39 tok/s)

Not checked: whether answers with the real image embeddings are better than before (acceptance rate with images), other backends, other `qwen4exp` quants.

### First Bad Commit

`781dbc5ac` (#30257). Last good: `v0.6.0` / `d81235049`.

### Relevant log output

(see the assert and backtrace above; full log: `server-master-crash-image.log`)

Unrelated warnings that also appear on v0.6.0: `find_slot: non-consecutive token position 4 after 3 for sequence 0 with 64 new tokens`.

### Possibly related

#30032 (qwen4exp QSA indexer OOM when vision is active) is a different problem with the same model family and vision.

### Attachment

`qwen4exp-remove-assert.patch`:

```diff
--- a/src/models/qwen4exp.cpp
+++ b/src/models/qwen4exp.cpp
@@ -526,7 +526,6 @@ llama_model_qwen4exp::graph_mtp::graph_mtp(...)
     GGML_ASSERT(hparams.n_layer_nextn == 1 && "qwen4exp MTP has a single block");
-    GGML_ASSERT(ubatch.token && "qwen4exp MTP requires token input");
```
hints:
Still reproduces on master `08ffba21e` on Apple Silicon (M5 Max, Metal). The model is unsloth `UD-IQ4_XS` with `mmproj-BF16` and the self-contained Q8_0 MTP head, run with `--spec-type draft-mtp`. A single image request aborts the server with the same `qwen4exp.cpp:529` assert.

#30316 fixes it on the same machine, with no change on the text path. Details are in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30316.

query:
Misc. bug: Vulkan: ggml_backend_vk_get_device_memory reports free > total when the driver's heapBudget exceeds heap size (Intel iGPU, Windows); downstream consumers underflow

### Name and Version

ggml-vulkan as bundled in node-llama-cpp 3.20.0 (llama.cpp **b10361**, prebuilt `win-x64-vulkan`).
The function is unchanged on current master
([`4ceb171`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/4ceb1719101f32637b841206c172f3f058ffc182/ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L14878-L14909)).

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other: `ggml-vulkan` (`ggml_backend_vk_get_device_memory`, which is `ggml_backend_dev_memory` for Vulkan devices)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On an Intel integrated GPU under Windows, the driver reports a `VK_EXT_memory_budget` heap budget
**larger than the heap itself**. Windows `vulkaninfo`, Intel driver 101.8860, Arc B390, a single
`DEVICE_LOCAL` heap:

```
memoryHeaps[0]:
    size   = 38868971888 (36.20 GiB)
    budget = 50206003200 (46.76 GiB)
    usage  = 4096 (4.00 KiB)
```

That violates the spec (*"The `heapBudget` value **must** be less than or equal to
`VkMemoryHeap::size` for each heap"*,
[VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryBudgetPropertiesEXT](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryBudgetPropertiesEXT.html)),
so the root cause is the driver. `ggml_backend_vk_get_device_memory()` passes it straight through:

```cpp
*total += heap.size;                                             // 36.20 GiB
if (membudget_supported && i < budgetprops.heapUsage.size()) {
    *free += budgetprops.heapBudget[i] - budgetprops.heapUsage[i]; // 46.76 GiB
}
```

The result is **`free > total`**: 46.76 GiB free of 36.20 GiB. Any consumer that computes
`used = total - free` in unsigned arithmetic then wraps. node-llama-cpp does exactly that. It reports
`used = 2^64 - 11.34 GB`, clamps free VRAM to 0, offloads 0 layers, and fails every context with
`A context size of 2048 is too large for the available VRAM`, even at 512
([withcatai/node-llama-cpp#653](https://github.com/withcatai/node-llama-cpp/issues/653)). The
arithmetic reconciles exactly: 36.20 GiB − 46.76 GiB = −11,337,027,216 B.

A second, related hazard sits on the same line. `heapBudget[i] - heapUsage[i]` is itself unsigned
(`VkDeviceSize`). If a driver ever reports `usage > budget`, which the spec permits (the budget is "a
rough estimate" and usage can exceed it under pressure), then `free` wraps **inside ggml**.

**Suggested fix:** clamp at the source, so `ggml_backend_dev_memory` always returns `0 <= free <= total`:

```cpp
const vk::DeviceSize budget = std::min(budgetprops.heapBudget[i], heap.size);
const vk::DeviceSize usage  = budgetprops.heapUsage[i];
*free += budget > usage ? budget - usage : 0;
```

**Why here as well as downstream:** consumers reasonably assume `ggml_backend_dev_memory` returns
`free <= total`. A clamp in ggml protects every consumer at once: node-llama-cpp, llama.cpp's own
memory fitting, and the tools built on either. The Windows Intel driver is not the only
implementation that could return an out-of-spec budget.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Windows 11, Intel iGPU (seen here on Arc B390 with driver 32.0.101.8860; the same symptom appeared
   on 32.0.101.8724).
2. Run `vulkaninfo` and confirm `budget > size` for the device-local heap.
3. Call `ggml_backend_dev_memory()` on the Vulkan device. It returns `free` ≈ 50.2e9 and
   `total` ≈ 38.9e9.

**Cross-checks**

- The same GPU through Mesa Dozen (`dzn`, Mesa 26.2.2) under WSL2 reports sane values: 23.5 GB free of
  47.5 GB. Downstream offload works normally there, which isolates the problem to the Windows Intel
  driver's budget value.
- A downstream report shows the same failure chain on a different Intel iGPU:
  [tobi/qmd#969](https://github.com/tobi/qmd/issues/969), Intel UHD 770 with driver 32.0.101.7088,
  `VRAM 0 B free`. That suggests the out-of-spec budget spans Intel driver generations.
- Once the budget check is bypassed downstream (`ignoreMemorySafetyChecks`), the device runs
  correctly. All layers are offloaded and results match CPU. So only the memory **reporting** is wrong.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. The subtraction arrived with the memory-budget support in #15545; builds before it
returned `free = heap.size` and could not exceed `total`.

### Relevant log output

```
# node-llama-cpp `inspect gpu`, Windows, b10361
Vulkan device: Intel(R) Arc(TM) B390 GPU
Vulkan used VRAM: 47458790820.41% (16384PB/36.2GB)
Vulkan free VRAM: 0% (0B/36.2GB)
Vulkan unified memory: 36.2GB (100%)
```

Misc. bug: ~7% slower CPU-side MoE decode on AVX2+F16C (i7-10750H) since #30270 (b11555): Clang lowers the scalar F16C conversion to a vpinsrw merge on the accumulator

### Name and Version

Official Windows nightlies (`llama-bNNNNN-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip` + cudart zip, CI build with Clang 20.1.8). CPU backend loaded at runtime: `ggml-cpu-haswell.dll` (SSE42 AVX F16C FMA AVX2 BMI2).

```
build 11553 (62a6f74ba)  OK
build 11554 (966baae76)  OK
build 11555 (1cf776776)  ~7% slower token generation (CPU-side experts), kernel 1.5-1.65x slower
build 11556 (a9d27ac69)  same as 11555
```

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

ggml-cpu (`simd-mappings.h`, scalar FP16->FP32 conversion used by the quantized dot products)

### Command line

```
llama-bench.exe -m Ornith-1.5-35B-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 999 -t 6 -fa on -b 4096 -ub 2048 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -ncmoe 99 -p 2048 -n 128 -r 5 --prio 2 -o jsonl
test-backend-ops.exe perf -b CPU -o MUL_MAT_ID -p "type_a=q8_0,.*n_mats=128.*,n=1,k=2048"
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hardware: Intel i7-10750H (Comet Lake: AVX2 + FMA + F16C, no AVX-512), 2x32 GB DDR4-2933, RTX 2060 (attention on CUDA, experts on CPU with `-ncmoe 99`). Model: Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B Q8_0 (qwen35moe, 3B active).

**1. Bisection with official nightlies** (alternating order, GGUF warm, tg128 mean of 3 reps per pass): b11553 14.56 t/s, b11554 14.79, b11555 13.67, b11556 13.54. No prompt-processing drop attributable to the PR in this full configuration (332-336 t/s, prefill carried by the GPU); the CPU-only prefill-shaped kernel case does slow down (see 2). The only commit between b11554 and b11555 is 1cf776776 (#30270).

**2. Same compiler, only the CPU DLL changes.** Three builds of `ggml-cpu-haswell.dll` from 1cf776776 with Clang 20.1.8 and the `windows-cpu` CI recipe (`GGML_NATIVE=OFF`, `GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`, `GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON`, OpenMP), dropped into copies of the official b11555 folder (CUDA, llama-bench, ggml-base identical): **A** = #30270 reverted, **B** = intact, **C** = only the `#define GGML_CPU_FP16_TO_FP32(x) GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_FP16_TO_FP32(x)` line removed (the `FP32_TO_FP16` one kept). `__F16C__` verified defined for the haswell variant (`-O3 -msse4.2 -mavx -mf16c -mfma -mavx2 -mbmi2`).

llama-bench, 45 s cooldown between runs, order B-C-A-B-A-C, 5 reps each (steady-state samples, first sample is a turbo burst):

| run | variant | tg128 mean | samples |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | B | 14.03 | 15.19 13.89 13.65 13.69 13.70 |
| 2 | C | 14.63 | 15.90 14.43 14.15 14.39 14.27 |
| 3 | A | 14.81 | 16.09 14.63 14.48 14.44 14.41 |
| 4 | B | 13.81 | 14.92 13.75 13.23 13.63 13.52 |
| 5 | A | 14.83 | 16.12 14.61 14.40 14.55 14.46 |
| 6 | C | 14.82 | 16.13 14.58 14.38 14.56 14.45 |

test-backend-ops perf, CPU only, MUL_MAT_ID (128 experts, 8 used, n=1), min of 8 alternating rounds, us/op: q8_0 A 340 / B 493 / C 332 (kernel time +45%); q4_0 A 265 / B 398 / C 267 (+50%). Prefill-shaped case (q8_0, n=512): A 72.7 ms / B 179.7 ms / C 70.0 ms. No consistent slowdown detected in the tested iq4_xs, iq2_xs, f16 and K-quant cases.

**3. Mechanism.** Disassembly of `ggml_vec_dot_q8_0_q8_0` (haswell object). Before the PR (A, C) the per-block scale conversion is a table load (`movzwl` + `vmovss (%r11,%rsi,4)`). With the PR (B), the compiled branch is the `_MSC_VER` one (Clang defines `_MSC_VER` for the windows-msvc target), i.e. `_mm_cvtss_f32(_mm_cvtph_ps(_mm_cvtsi32_si128(x)))`, which Clang lowers to

```
vpinsrw $0, (%r9,%r10), %xmm0, %xmm2 ; vcvtph2ps %xmm2, %xmm2
vpinsrw $0, (%rax,%r10), %xmm0, %xmm3 ; vcvtph2ps %xmm3, %xmm3
...
vfmadd231ps %ymm3, %ymm2, %ymm0
```

`vpinsrw` merges into `%xmm0`, and `%ymm0` is the loop accumulator written by `vfmadd231ps`, so every iteration depends on the previous one. `llvm-mca -mcpu=skylake` (model estimates, not hardware counters): A 4.3 cycles/iteration (IPC 3.52); B 19.1 cycles/iteration (IPC 0.84, "register dependencies 90.7%"); B with a distinct zero register in the two `vpinsrw` (hand-edited asm) 5.2 cycles. A standalone mock-up of the dot product compiled with the same flags confirms this on hardware: table 1.36-1.47 ns/block, F16C with the merge (what Clang emits) 4.56-4.71 ns/block (3.3x), F16C without the merge (forced `vmovd` + `vcvtph2ps` via inline asm, experiment only) 1.47-1.56 ns/block. The F16C intrinsic itself is not slow; the false loop-carried dependency is. Every single-scalar source form tried (`_cvtsh_ss`, `_mm_cvtsi32_si128`, `_mm_set_epi32(0,0,0,h)`, `_mm_set1_epi16`, `_mm_loadu_si16`, insert into `_mm_setzero_si128()`) is canonicalised by Clang 20.1.8 to the same `vpinsrw` merge. Converting both block scales at once (`x.d | y.d << 16` → `_mm_cvtsi32_si128` → one `_mm_cvtph_ps` → `_mm_shuffle_ps`) does avoid it with the same compiler (`vmovd` + `vcvtph2ps` + `vmovshdup`, 1.56-1.64 ns/block in the mock-up, bit-exact on the 1800 finite random inputs tested), but that means rewriting the kernels where a paired conversion fits, not a drop-in for the scalar macro.

Scope: one CPU, one compiler version tested; MSVC proper not affected (`__F16C__` is never defined there); GCC and other toolchains not tested. Proposed minimal fix: keep the F16C path for `GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16` (the PR's stated goal) and the lookup table for `GGML_CPU_FP16_TO_FP32` on x86 (variant C above). Variant C recovers most of the loss and overlaps the reverted build within our measurement noise; strict equality is not established.

load_backend: loaded CPU backend from ggml-cpu-haswell.dll

query:
server: prompt cache is populated by rerank tasks that can never read it back (cache_idle_slots missing the SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION guard)

### Summary

On a rerank-only server, host RAM grows by ~23 MB per `/v1/rerank` call until it reaches the `--cache-ram` limit (8192 MiB by default), and is never released while the process lives. The growth is the **prompt cache being populated by rerank tasks that can never read it back** - for `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_RERANK` the cache is write-only.

This is not the same as #25740 (closed as not-planned). There the cache was doing its job on the completion path and the reporter simply hadn't set `-cram 0`. Here the entries are provably never read, so the memory is pure waste plus a per-request serialisation cost.

### Version / environment

- `b4d6c7d8ff69c2e05e4e8ee7e6e710a08abd7b45` (b10091), also present on master at time of writing
- CUDA, aarch64 (NVIDIA GB10), driver 580.173.02
- Model: Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B Q8_0 GGUF
- Server: `llama-server --reranking --pooling rank -c 8192 -np 2 -ngl 999 -fa on --no-mmap`
- Reproduced identically on two hosts

### The path

1. `POST /v1/rerank` creates independent `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_RERANK` tasks with no parent.
2. `server_slot::release()` clears the prompt only for child tasks (`server-context.cpp:488-491`):
   ```cpp
   // do not keep context of the child slots - the parent's context is enough
   if (task->is_child()) {
       prompt_clear();
   }
   ```
   Rerank tasks are not children, so `slot.prompt` and its KV state survive release.
3. On the next task launch, the idle-slot pass saves every idle slot to the prompt cache (`server-context.cpp:2398-2414`) - **with no task-type guard**:
   ```cpp
   if (params_base.cache_idle_slots) {
       for (auto & slot : slots) {
           if (!slot.is_processing()) {
               if (slot.prompt_save(*prompt_cache)) {
   ```
4. The other call site does have the guard it needs (`server-context.cpp:1617-1618`):
   ```cpp
   // cache prompts only for completion tasks
   update_cache = update_cache && task.type == SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION;
   ```
5. `prompt_load` is only reached from inside that completion-gated branch, so nothing ever reads a rerank entry back.

With `-np 2`, `kv_unified` is false, so the `[TAG_IDLE_SLOT_CLEAR]` path does not run and the slot keeps its prompt after the save as well.

### Measurements

Fresh restart each arm, 40 calls, resident memory of the service:

| workload | growth |
|---|---|
| 40 calls, **identical** query+docs | +68 MB, then flat from call ~10 |
| 40 calls, 20 docs, **40 distinct** doc lengths | +3032 MB by call 20, climbing until capped |
| same, with `--cache-ram 0` | +626 MB |
| same, `--cache-ram 0` + `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | +620 MB (graph cache not involved) |
| same 40 lengths **descending** | +620 MB immediately, then flat |

Two separate effects: the cache (dominant, content-keyed, deduped only on full prefix match, so every distinct query+document pair is a new entry) and a benign high-water-mark buffer allocation of ~620 MB that stops growing once the largest request has been seen.

The arithmetic matches: Qwen3-0.6B is 28 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim, f16 → 112 KiB/token, so ~23 MB/call ≈ 210 tokens of KV state - a query plus a few short documents. In production the process sat at 9137 MB with **zero busy slots**, consistent with ~1.1 GB baseline plus the 8 GiB cap.

### Reproduce

```bash
llama-server -m Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf --reranking --pooling rank -c 8192 -np 2
# then POST /v1/rerank repeatedly with DIFFERENT documents each time and watch RSS.
# Identical documents will not reproduce it - the cache dedups on full prefix match.
```

### Suggested fix

Apply the same guard the completion path already uses, so idle slots are only saved for task types that can read the cache back:

```cpp
if (params_base.cache_idle_slots) {
    for (auto & slot : slots) {
        if (!slot.is_processing() && slot.task && slot.task->type == SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION) {
```

Alternatively (or additionally) clear the prompt on release for task types that never reuse it.

### Workaround

`--cache-ram 0` (which also auto-disables `cache_idle_slots`), or `--no-cache-idle-slots`. For a rerank/embedding-only server this costs nothing, since those entries are never read. Confirmed: 9137 MB → ~1.1 GB steady state on our fleet.

### Note on scope

`/v1/embeddings` builds non-child `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_EMBEDDING` tasks through the same `send_embedding` → `release()` path, so it looks structurally exposed. I could **not** reproduce growth on an embedding-only server (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 30 distinct input lengths, +20 MB and flat), so I am reporting only what I measured rather than assuming.
hints:
Adding the measurements behind this, since the report above was mostly a code-reading and the numbers make the cost concrete.

Setup: `llama-server` as a reranker (`--reranking`), `qwen3-reranker-0.6b` Q8_0, GB10 / CUDA 13 / aarch64. Fresh restart per arm, 40 rerank calls per arm, RSS sampled with zero busy slots.

## Measured decomposition

| workload | RSS growth |
|---|---|
| 40 calls, **identical** content | +68 MB, then flat from call ~10 |
| 40 calls, **distinct** content | **+3,032 MB by call 20**, still climbing until the cap |
| distinct content, `--cache-ram 0` | **+626 MB** |
| distinct content, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | +620 MB |
| same lengths, **descending** | +620 MB immediately, then flat |

Three things fall out of that:

1. **Identical content is flat, distinct content grows.** That is the signature of a cache keyed on prompt content that nothing ever reads back, rather than an allocator leak.
2. **`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` changes nothing** (+620 vs +626 MB), so the CUDA graph cache is ruled out as the source.
3. **Descending lengths grow once and then stay flat**, so the ~620 MB residual is a benign high-water mark, not an ongoing leak.

The arithmetic matches the KV interpretation: Qwen3-0.6B is 28 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim at f16 = **112 KiB/token**, so ~23 MB/call is about 210 tokens of KV state per rerank call.

## What it cost in production

The unit had been running for weeks and sat at **9,137 MB RSS with zero busy slots**, which is consistent with roughly 1.1 GB of baseline plus the full 8 GiB `--cache-ram` default being filled with entries that can never be hit.

Adding `--cache-ram 0`:

| host | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| A | 9,137 MB | **1,194 MB** |
| B | 9,137 MB | **561 MB** |

Those readings have held since. Sampling the same units today, weeks later, gives 1,094 MB and 199 MB, so the fixed state is stable and the residual really is the high-water mark rather than a slower leak.

## Negative control

**The embedder does not share the defect**, and this was measured rather than assumed: `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` over 30 distinct input lengths grew **+20 MB and stayed flat**. `/v1/embeddings` looks structurally exposed through the same non-completion path, but it did not reproduce, so whatever guards it in practice may be worth comparing against the rerank path.

## One implementation note

`--cache-ram 0` is a complete workaround rather than a partial one, because it also turns off the idle-slot publish. In `server-context.cpp`:

```
if (params_base.cache_idle_slots) {
    if (params_base.cache_ram_mib == 0) {
        SRV_WRN("%s", "--cache-idle-slots requires --cache-ram, disabling\n");
        params_base.cache_idle_slots = false;
```

So a reranker deployment can mitigate today with the single flag, at no cost, since the cache was never readable for these tasks anyway. That said, the default is on, and a rerank-only server silently giving up 8 GiB of RAM to unreachable entries is a poor default.

`#26893` ("server: avoid caching non-completion idle slots in RAM") looks like it addresses this. Happy to test a patch on the workload above, the distinct-content arm reproduces in well under a minute.

This also affects embedding-only servers. There it shows up as falling throughput rather than memory growth (~2 KB per input), which may be why the 30-input test above looked flat.

**Setup:** build 11026 (`b49650adb`; the same code is on master at `4b1a27fa0`), Vulkan on an AMD Radeon 8060S (RADV), bge-m3 FP16 (an encoder, no KV memory).
`llama-server --embeddings --pooling cls -ngl 99 -c 8192 -b 8192 -ub 8192 --parallel 8`
One client posts `/v1/embeddings` with 32 distinct inputs at a time, back to back (~50 inputs/s).

| uptime | inputs/min |
|---|---|
| 0 | ~2,950 |
| 30 min | ~2,200 |
| 6 h 47 min | ~400 (GPU ~22% busy at ~1 GHz) |

A restart restores the full rate immediately. RSS grows ~5 MB/min.

**Why the limits never evict:** each entry's state (`llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`) is ~0 bytes, so `size()` never approaches `--cache-ram`. In `update()`, `size_per_token = max(1.0f, size()/n_tokens())` is then 1, so `limit_tokens_cur = limit_size / 1`, about 8.6e9 tokens. `states` gains one entry per distinct input for the life of the process.

Each launch offers every idle slot to the cache (non-unified KV with `--parallel 8`, so slots keep their prompt). Each offer walks the whole list: in `alloc()` twice (the duplicate check, then contained-prompt removal), and again in `update()` (`size()` and `n_tokens()`). The cost per input grows linearly with the inputs served, on the thread that feeds the GPU.

**Workaround:** `--cache-ram 0`, which also disables `cache_idle_slots`. With it, over 45 min of uptime: ~3,040 inputs/min at 0-10 min, ~3,040 at 30 min, ~2,930 at 45 min (every minute fell between 2,912 and 3,072). RSS growth dropped from ~5 MB/min to ~1.2 MB/min; I haven't identified the rest.

**Fix:** the task-type guard proposed above covers this. Separately, the byte-derived token limit in `update()` shouldn't apply when the saved state is ~0 bytes.

The decision endpoint (`/v1/systemone`) has the same problem, and on decision models it costs throughput as well as RAM. `get_available_slot()` only restores from the cache for completion tasks, but the idle-slot save in `process_single_task()` runs after every task, including `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_DECISION`. So on a decision-only server the cache is write-only: our `-lv 4` traces show 0 restores in every run.

Measured on current master (fcac190), one RTX 5090, 104 `/v1/systemone` requests with 5 questions each (half short, half ~2k-token states; half sent one at a time, half with 4 in flight), 3 fresh-server runs per setting. Decisions/s, mean ± sd:

| Model | `-np` | default | `--cache-ram 0` | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kev-4B 2.5 GB GGUF | 8 | 15.90 ± 0.15 | 19.98 ± 0.17 | 1.26x |
| Kev-4B 2.5 GB GGUF | 16 | 14.39 ± 0.29 | 17.64 ± 0.23 | 1.23x |
| Kev-4B BF16 | 8 | 15.18 ± 0.05 | 18.49 ± 0.59 | 1.22x |
| Kev-9B 4.8 GB GGUF | 8 | 14.44 ± 0.09 | 17.29 ± 0.07 | 1.20x |
| pplx-decider 27B 15.3 GB GGUF | 8 | 7.32 ± 0.09 | 9.39 ± 0.40 | 1.28x |
| pplx-decider 27B 15.3 GB GGUF | 16 | 7.02 ± 0.56 | 9.44 ± 0.47 | 1.34x |

`--no-cache-idle-slots` gives the same numbers as `--cache-ram 0`. At `-np 1` and `-np 4`, and with the default slot setting, there is no difference, because few idle slots hold an uncached prompt there. Clef-Flash is unaffected at every `-np`: its saved state is close to zero bytes. Answers at `-np 8` are bitwise identical with the cache on and off.

From the traces of one full run (104 requests, 520 decision tasks): at `-np 8`, Kev-4B makes 103 real saves (8.9 GiB copied to host, 6.5 to 8.4 s of save time, close to the wall-time difference between the two settings), and pplx-decider makes 82 saves (18.5 GiB, 15.1 s). Host RSS at `-np 8` is 12.9 GB with the default against 4.4 GB with the cache off, because the cache fills its 8 GiB limit.

The guard suggested in this issue would fix decision tasks too: skip the idle-slot save unless the slot's last task was a completion, the same condition `get_available_slot()` already uses. Until then `--cache-ram 0` or `--no-cache-idle-slots` is the workaround for decision servers. Commands, full tables (`-np` 1 to 16, five models) and trace logs are available if useful.

Qwen3.8 27B, `llama-server` with `--ctx-checkpoints 32`.

Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 0f3a71b)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Reproduced against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` commit `0f3a71be15af836d277c9f918adfafb45732677e`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on \
  --slot-save-path /slot-cache
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.
