### Issue description

When attempting to set the "Root Type" import property of a model to a custom global class, the importer dialog will set the property value to the path (`res://...`) of the script file, *not* its global class name.

This results in the message "Cannot get class 'res://whatever/etc'." being displayed in the console. Trying to instantiate the imported model will not use the custom type.

This does not occur when using built-in classes. Only custom ones.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create or locate a 3D model file of any kind that can be imported by Godot.
2. Create a new script, in either GDScript or C#. The script must be a global class.
3. Edit the import settings of the model file. In its "Root Type" property, select your custom global class.
4. The value of the property will be set to a `res://` path instead of the name of the class. An error will be raised in the console `Cannot get class 'res://whatever/etc'.`


This can be bypassed by editing the `.import` file by hand, and replacing the value of `nodes/root_type` to a string of the class's global name, as opposed to its path.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[custom_type_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31184536/custom_type_repro.zip) includes a scene with a cube attached to a single armature. The import settings of this model are set to the custom type as defined by GDScript. The two custom node types are called `CustomType` and `CustomTypeButGDScript` for C# and GDScript respectively. Select either of these two for the "Root Type" property to cause the error.

Metal: Vulkan: ``` Godot v4.7.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.5.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ``` I am seeing this as well on 4.7 stable. macOS 26.5.1 M5 Pro Both reproductions appear to be on M5 hardware, if we can get more tests on various chip generations this could help confirm what hardware this occurs on, will post in the Godot contributors chat. Unfortunately this limitation may make it hard to find someone able to investigate the issue further who also has affected hardware. Unable to reproduce on a standard M4 processor (13 inch MacBook Air, 2025) using the default metal driver. SDFGI appears to be working as expected, even when background/ambient lighting is disabled: Default settings: `background_energy_multiplier` set to 0: Additionally, I can reproduce the issue on a M5 MacBook Air. ``` Godot Engine v4.7.1.stable.mono.official.a13da4feb - https://godotengine.org Metal 4.0 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: Apple - Apple M5 (Apple9) ``` Setting `Driver.macos` to `vulkan` corrects the issue. 3 reports confirm on M5, with 2 disconfirming reports on M1 and M4, so this does seem like something specific with the M5 generation of chips - have marked as confirmed but this could be difficult to figure out if there isn't a contributor with the correct hardware I don't have any M5 hardware to validate and fix this issue (M1 and M4 only) I took a look into this and noticed a potential cause: the voxelization shader updates `render_geom_facing` using [`imageAtomicOr()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5d63a641c79b5fb83e8d6752864c739f3254d720/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L2937-L2941), but [`gi.cpp` creates the texture without `TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5d63a641c79b5fb83e8d6752864c739f3254d720/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L454-L459). Bisecting between `4.4.1-stable` (working) and `4.5-stable` (broken) led to commit [`5230f6c60c`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/5230f6c60c28b1a34fb0136f84aa901afe382f39) in PR #108028 (*"Apple: Use image atomic operations on supported Apple hardware"*): - **Before #108028**: The Metal driver automatically added `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` to any texture whose pixel format supported atomics. - **After #108028**: It only sets `MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic` when `TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT` is explicitly requested. Volumetric fog textures were updated with this bit, but `render_geom_facing` was missed. - Vulkan storage images and D3D12 UAV textures implicitly permit atomics, but Metal strictly requires [`MTLTextureUsageShaderAtomic`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtltextureusage/shaderatomic). Without it, atomic operations on Apple9 fail silently. Adding the missing usage flag in `gi.cpp`: ```diff diff --git a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp @@ -454,6 +454,8 @@ tf_render.format = RD::DATA_FORMAT_R32_UINT; + tf_render.usage_bits |= RD::TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT; render_geom_facing = create_clear_texture(tf_render, "SDFGI Render Geometry Facing"); + tf_render.usage_bits &= ~RD::TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_ATOMIC_BIT; ``` Tested on an Apple M5 Max and it solve the issue. *(Note: It's still unclear why Apple7 / M1 was more forgiving and tolerated the missing flag).*

query: AnimationMixer applies Node3D scale animation tracks in parent space when combining position/rotation/scale ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: Godot 4.7-stable (4.7 branch, commit 1a5d818ea97) - Not reproducible in: Godot 4.6.3-stable ### System information Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - Godot v4.7.0 (custom build, 4.7 branch, commit 1a5d818ea97) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (nvidia, driver version unknown) - 13th Gen Intel Core i5-13600KF (16 Threads) ### Issue description When an Animation has `position_3d`, `rotation_3d`, and `scale_3d` tracks targeting the same Node3D node (standard glTF TRS import), Godot 4.7 applies the transform differently than 4.6.3, causing incorrect visual results. Symptoms: - The Inspector `Scale` value for the animated node no longer matches the original keyframe values. - Child nodes (MeshInstance3D, GPUParticles3D) are visibly distorted due to unexpected basis composition. - Particle AABBs are deformed by the parent node's incorrect transform. The root cause is in commit `1a5d818ea9` ("Optimize AnimationTree & Improve internals"). In `AnimationMixer::_blend_apply()`, the previous code called `set_position()` / `set_rotation()` / `set_scale()` separately; the optimization merged them into a single `set_transform()` when all three tracks are present: ```cpp // 4.7 problematic code Transform3D transform = Transform3D(Basis(t->rot).scaled(t->scale), t->loc); t_node_3d->set_transform(transform); ``` `Basis::scaled()` operates in **parent/global space (multiplies rows)**, but `Node3D.scale` and the animation `TYPE_SCALE_3D` track are defined as **local space (multiplies columns)**. The correct equivalent is `Basis::scaled_local()`. In 4.6, the separate setters eventually went through `Node3D::_update_local_transform()` → `Basis::set_euler_scale()`, which internally performs `R * S` (diagonal scale matrix then rotation), matching local scale semantics — same as `scaled_local()`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. In Blender, create a node with non-uniform scale (e.g. `(2.5, 1.0, 2.5)`) and rotation. 2. Bake keyframes for position, rotation, and scale (standard glTF TRS animation). 3. Export as GLB and import into a Godot project. 4. Attach a child MeshInstance3D or GPUParticles3D under that node. 5. Play the animation, or simply select the node in the editor and compare the Inspector `Scale` against the original keyframe values — they will differ. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animation-issue-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29879649/animation-issue-mrp.zip)

Therefore there shouldn't be autocompletion for them. But there is (showing constants from the same enum): I don't see why this is needed for anything (especially since it gives an error: `Cannot get property from enum value.`), so it's clearly a bug. hints:
I think I've got a fix for this!

From my investigation, the problem seemed to be that the parent expression of `KEY_0` was being recognized as an enum type, and as a result it was also assigning the enum type to `KEY_0` itself. As a result, when you typed `KEY_0.` it wanted to suggest possible enum values for the enum type that `KEY_0` belonged to.

My notes:

> C++ enum values and user-defined enum values have `r_type.kind = 0 (GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN)` and `builtin_type = 2 (Variant::INT)`
> Example:
> ```gdscript
> enum { ONE, TWO }
> enum MyEnum { THREE, FOUR }
> ...
> var i = KEY_0. <-- int
> var j = Key.KEY_0. <-- int
> var k = ONE. <-- int
> var l = MyEnum.THREE. <-- int
> ```
> (Note that `Key` by itself is not considered a constant, apparently.)
> 
> User-defined named enums' names have `r_type.kind = 0 (GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN)` and `builtin_type = 27 (Variant::DICTIONARY)`
> Example:
> ```gdscript
> enum MyEnum { ONE, TWO }
> ...
> var i = MyEnum. <--- 
> var j = MyEnum.ONE <-- (no period after name)
> ```

I am able to stop the bad behavior without (to my testing so far) introducing any new bad behavior and with minimal, self-contained changes to `gdscript_editor.cpp` - will open a PR for them soon.

query:
Can cause "Compiler bug: Unresolved return" with await and inheritance

### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.70 and 4.7.1

Was not encountered in any previous version of Godot.

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.5.2) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

If you have a method that has a declared return type and contains an `await`:
```gdscript
class_name InheritThis

func returns_bool_with_await() -> bool:
    await get_tree().process_frame
    return true
```
If you override that method without specifying a return type, and it returns an undeterminable value:
```gdscript
class_name CausesError
extends InheritThis

func this_returns_whatever():
    return 'whatever'

func returns_bool_with_await():
    return await this_returns_whatever()
```
it will cause a `Compiler bug: Unresolved return` error when the script is loaded.
```
ERROR: Compiler bug: Unresolved return.
   at: write_return (modules/gdscript/gdscript_byte_codegen.cpp:1846)
```
This is a compile time error, but it does not prevent the script from being compiled and usable.

The source code ([in 4.7](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c050c09b105c3715e1caa57a7109cd752047fd89/modules/gdscript/gdscript_byte_codegen.cpp#L1845)) indicates that this condition should be unreachable.
```cpp
		case GDScriptDataType::VARIANT: {
			ERR_PRINT("Compiler bug: Unresolved return.");

			// Shouldn't get here, but fail-safe to a regular return.
			append_opcode(GDScriptFunction::OPCODE_RETURN);
			append(p_return_value);
		} break;
```

This has caused [an issue](https://github.com/bitwes/Gut/issues/842) in the [GUT](https://github.com/bitwes/Gut) unit testing framework.  Currently there is insufficient meta data for GUT to be able to determine the return type in all cases.  This error appears when users create doubles/mocks of objects that contain methods like `returns_bool_with_await`.  This can happen frequently in a test suite.


### Steps to reproduce

Loading/running the following script will cause the error.  I used `<godot> -s main.gd`.
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

class InheritThis:
	extends Node

	func returns_bool_with_await() -> bool:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		return true


class CausesError:
	extends InheritThis

	func this_returns_whatever():
		return 'whatever'
```

hints:
We'd have to change this in this version if we are going to, so marking as a priority

Bone Spreaders are also dental surgery tools to expand the ridge of narrowed alveolar bone, it seems 🤔.

If the meaning of the feature is to stretch, i.e. elongate, as opposed to separating two bones from a common joint for example, then the name is not only unfortunate and potentially unpleasant but wrong and misleading

@TokageItLab can you provide some context on what was meant by the name and what the intended functionality is?

The name of this modifier needs to be intended to show that it never scales bones, but rather repositions joints. Because scaling bones causes features like IK to be broken the behavior, we need to avoid names that imply scaling. Also, since it functions on its own, names related to Skin are not considered desirable.

Initially it was BoneExpander, but since that strongly gave the impression of performing scaling, it became Spreader, which strictly represents its action, that meaning that in 1 vs n bones, the position is "spread" by the value set in this node.

In other words, it's a position converter from scale. A name like "Scl2PosConverter3D" would probably be ideal, but it would break consistency with other Godot nodes. And the "Disperser" cannot be used because it is already in use by "BoneTwistDisperser3D".

Wouldn't "distributor" be more descriptive for that? Spread here wouldn't really describe what you describe what it does, the "out" part of "spread out" is not evident

> Wouldn't "distributor" be more descriptive for that? Spread here wouldn't really describe what you describe what it does, the "out" part of "spread out" is not evident

So how about "ChildBoneDistributor3D" or "ChildBoneRepositioner3D"? (I get the impression a bit that "Distributor" involves bone generation)

Distributor would be best I'd say, repositioner is a bit too generic, I wouldn't associate "distributor" with generating bones

We can then add "spread" or "spread out" as a keyword to the class

To confirm: it takes a chain of bones, like the arm of a character, and applies a scale so that the end of the bone chain is is scaled to a target and spreads the bones of the chain out between the positions, while not scaling the individual bones

Like having beads on a string and stretching it out ?

> Like having beads on a string and stretching it out?

That's probably right, but a more accurate description would be the feeling of smoothing out wrinkles when putting on clothes.

Then I'd say distributor would fit, though might be other words that fit better and might benefit from some further brainstorming

How about "ChildBoneSifter3D" ?

Did you mean shifter? That would be good too though a bit generic, either works I'd say

We we have:
* distributor
* repositioner
* shifter
* spreader (current name)

To me "spreader" either implies spreading like widening a joint like a V, or smearing out like butter, not so much to scatter or distribute

> To me "spreader" either implies spreading like widening a joint like a V

But, this is accurate. For example, if you change the width of the hand using `skin_scale`, you'll need to widen the spacing between the fingers. `BoneSpreader3D` serves the purpose of widening that spacing.

So the angle between the fingers changes? Not the relative positions

The angle remains the same. Even if you widen the "hand" skin, the roots of the fingers will remain in their original positions. BoneSpreader adjusts the position to increase the space between them.

The angle is what I meant by a "v", "spread" as opposed to "spread out", like spreading a fan or a hand of cards or an umbrella

Although the property's value “bone_pose_rotation“ remains unchanged, this means that the apparent angle of the line connecting the parent bone to the child bone will actually be spread.

Native English here and yes bone spreader is not ok.

BoneOffsetExtender
JointOffsetExtender

"Extender" was a candidate in the past, but I decided against it because it brings to mind scaling. I think we could distinguish it if it included "Offset", but since it doesn't apply an offset to a single bone, that would result in a very long class name: `ChildBoneOffsetExtender3D`.

Basically, what makes this a bit confusing is that, while it appears to be a scaling of the parent bone, what’s actually being applied is a change in the position of the child bone. So far, I personally feel that `ChildBoneShifter3D` is the short and most accurate.

query:
Seeking MP3 streams is slow at high offsets

### Tested versions

v4.7-beta.3
v4.6.3-stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable (35e80b3a8) - EndeavourOS #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 23 May 2026 14:21:20 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (nvidia; 580.159.04) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (6 threads) - 15.55 GiB memory

### Issue description

Doing seek operations on a MP3-based AudioStream is slow when seeking high offsets.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Import any long mp3 file.
2. Seek near the end (Seeking via the import settings preview does work).

Slowdown caused scales based on the audio bitrate, and the offset seeked.
(The MRP seeks 201 seconds in a MP3 file every frame, reporting the fps).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mp-3-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28241927/mp-3-bug.zip)
hints:
This isn't surprising, because the MP3 format doesn't have seek tables.
This means when encoded with VBR (variable bit-rate), it has to decode the entire file up to the target offset.
An article about the problem: https://valor-software.com/articles/diving-into-seeking-issue-with-mp3-files

I converted your MP3 to an Ogg Vorbis with FFmpeg:
```
ffmpeg -i "john stump - death waltz.mp3" "john stump - death waltz.ogg"
```
After that, your MRP went from 14 FPS to 60(+) FPS. Ogg Vorbis uses seek tables, so it's faster.
Note that converting from one lossy format to another will reduce the quality.

Footnote:
I also tried converting your MP3 to a CBR (constant bit-rate), which should be fast to seek (simply multiply bitrate by seek position). Sadly, the frame rate stays the same. This is probably because Godot doesn't know/check whether it's a CBR file.

I've been pondering seeking MP3s for a different reason(reverse playback). But it will come in handy here.
Some things I've learned:
- mp3 frames decode to exact number of audio samples: 1152.
- encoder gap is compensated using special frames(Xing/Info)
- VBR and CBR+reservoir are same thing, but data is arranged differently. One can be losslessly turned into the other. This means that only difference with VBR is having to pre-walk frames and index their start offsets to have good seek. And bit reservoir is just an offset from current frame.
- audio decoding DEPENDS on previous packets. If you try to decode two non-consecutive, you get sound soup.
- to get coherent sound, you need to pre-decode a number of frames before decoding your actual seek frame. This number depends on how stressed the decoder is at particular point in particular mp3 frame. Can be as little as 3, as high as 9 or more.

I've experimented in the name of reverse playback here: https://github.com/Polytoria/polytoria-game/issues/344#issuecomment-4472749076

And I will attach code of my experimentation.
OP's ache is solvable

https://gist.github.com/pachuco/8894f431f0048a9d63d10e46722687d9
Reverse playback experiment, which is pathological application of seeking(stress test).

Alternative I can think of is low-priority pre-computing seek tables for each mp3 sound asset on load.

This does not occur when using the editor's standard import process (outside the command line), or if resources are already imported in `.godot/`.

I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113051. cc @KoBeWi 

### Steps to reproduce

- Ensure the `.godot/` folder is *not* present in the project folder.
- Run `path/to/godot.binary --import --path /path/to/project`; it will always crash when `.godot/` is not present.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test_import_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32076606/test_import_crash.zip)

### Tested versions

Godot 4.7 stable

Macbook Air (M2, MacOS, 2022)

I am using an external editor (in my case Neovim) and attempting to connect to the LSP hosted by an open Godot instance. The LSP attaches every time, except when the project is in a path which features brackets -> [folder]/GameProject/etc.

In my Neovim instance, I get this:
`LSP[gdscript] The GDScript Language Server might not work correctly with other projects than the one opened in Godot.`

Setup an external editor and get working `server.pipe` communication, then open a project whose path includes a left or right bracket -> [ or ]

Often the result of creating a texture view from `texture_create_shared`. There is no compare against 0 anywhere in the function. The POOL path: allocationSize returns 0 (guards NO_SPACE), then `free()` indexes `m_nodes[0xffffffff]` and faults. Apple clang keeps the branch. Unclear yet whether upstream clang is mis-compiling or performing some other optimisation. Summary from 🤖 (and my edits) after comparing Apple clang output with llvm@21. The root cause is not a compiler bug. Undefined behaviour in metal-cpp's `NS::SharedPtr`, exploited by upstream LLVM but not by Apple clang. **Mechanism** `~SharedPtr` in `thirdparty/metal-cpp/Foundation/NSSharedPtr.hpp` line 170: ```cpp _NS_INLINE NS::SharedPtr<_Class>::~SharedPtr<_Class>() __attribute__((no_sanitize("undefined"))) { m_pObject->release(); } ``` No null check. Calling a member function through a null pointer is UB. Clang tags `this` as `nonnull`. In `_free_allocation`, `old_heap` is a default-constructed `SharedPtr`, and on the `INVALID` path it is provably null at the destructor. LLVM concludes that path is unreachable and deletes the `case INVALID` edge. Every remaining path locks a pool, so the lock gets hoisted above the switch. Result: `INVALID` handles fall into the POOL path, `free(NO_SPACE)` indexes `m_nodes[0xffffffff]`, crash. The `no_sanitize("undefined")` attribute suppresses the sanitizer, not the optimizer. > [!IMPORTANT] > > `m_pObject->release()` is not actually UB, as Apple's Metal headers don't ever dereference `this`. All calls are through Objective-C message send, and it is valid to send a message to a `nil` object in Objective-C: > > https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c24bf5d933c53d9477d5e82c51403856a9e7da62/thirdparty/metal-cpp/Foundation/NSObject.hpp#L113-L117 > > `this` only passes the pointer, and the Objective-C runtime checks for `nil` and simply returns. **How the 🤖 validated it** - Homebrew clang 21.1.8, `-O3`, main's source: reproduces official codegen exactly. Same at `-O1`, `-O2`, `-Os`. - `-O0` IR still has the full three-way switch. The optimizer removes it. - Apple clang 21.0.0, identical flags: keeps the branch. Matches the CI binary you provided, which also ran clean. - `-fno-delete-null-pointer-checks` with clang 21: branch restored. - Null check added to `~SharedPtr` only, clang 21: branch restored. **Other unguarded derefs in the same header**, all potentially the same hazard: | Line | Function | | -------- | -------------------- | | 170 | destructor | | 181 | copy constructor | | 228 | `reset()` | | 243 | copy assignment | | 269, 275 | `operator=` variants | | 288 | move assignment | **The 🤖 recommended the following fix** Guard every `m_pObject->` call in `NSSharedPtr.hpp` with a null check, shipped as a metal-cpp patch. Safer than `-fno-delete-null-pointer-checks` because any default-constructed `SharedPtr` destroyed on a provably-null path anywhere in the driver can hit this. The `_free_allocation` early return I suggested earlier only masks this one site. I'm still evaluating solutions, as there are a few.

### Issue description

Opening the Editor after the Commit dock was closed opens the Version Control dock. The only way to close it is to open the Commit dock from the menu and then close it.

Loading a layout with the Commit dock opened or closed does not correspondingly open or close the Version Control dock. 
The signals are not correct here, I think `closed` only make sense to use for transient docks since they don't close when loading layouts. I'm not sure what the `opened` signal would be useful for since it doesn't handle everywhere it opens. We should probably deprecate it so users don't try to rely on it for code that needs to run when their dock opens.
The `closed` signal documentation can also be updated to clarify the dock may close in other ways.
Or we can update the signals to just emit in every case they are opened or closed.

Also it would be great if the Version Control dock could be closed directly since it is more visible than the Commit dock which by default gets hidden behind the other docks in its slot. It's fine to set it as closable, it automatically opens when needed, and users can finish using it while still wanting the Commit dock open.

The Version Control dock should also be closed by default and only opened when the Commit dock needs it, rather than when the Commit dock opens IMO. It doesn't show anything by default, so its not useful to have open until something is selected in the Commit dock.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Setup VCS
2. Close the Commit dock (which closes the Version Control dock)
3. Reload the editor (avoiding https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107089)
4. The Version Control dock is open but the Commit dock is closed, and it cannot directly be closed.

For layouts 
1. Add an editor layout with the Commit dock open
2. Close the Commit dock
3. Add an editor layout with the Commit dock closed
4. Load the opened layout, see that the Version Control dock does not open
5. Manually close and reopen from the menu
6. Load the closed layout, see that the Version Control dock does not close

query:
Engine segfaults on exit if a CanvasTexture RID is leaked

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.4.stable, 4.5.stable, 4.6.stable, 4.7.stable, 4.7.1.stable, 4.7.2.stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.0.stable, 4.1.stable, 4.2.2.stable, 4.3.stable. The CanvasTexture still leaks in those, the engine just exits cleanly.

### System information

macOS 27.0 - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Forward+ (Metal 4.0) - Apple M3 Pro

### Issue description

If a CanvasTexture RID is still allocated when the engine shuts down, Godot segfaults instead of just printing the usual `RID allocations of type ... were leaked at exit`.

I ran into it with a dual-grid TileMapLayer addon that leaks a TileSet along with its CanvasTextures. The editor crashed every time I closed it, restarted it, or went back to the project list, and it took me a while to connect that to the leak. The MRP does the same thing the simple way: drops a Sprite2D out of the tree without freeing it.

The cleanup loop in `~RID_Alloc` destroys the leaked elements, so `~CanvasTexture` runs and fires its `invalidated_callback`. That callback belongs to `RendererCanvasRenderRD`, which is already gone by then: `RendererCompositorRD::finalize()` deletes the canvas renderer before the texture storage, so `RendererCanvasRender::singleton` is null and the callback dereferences null. `~RendererCanvasRenderRD` does clear this callback for `default_canvas_texture`. Just not for anything in `canvas_texture_to_uniform_set`.

Side effect: the crash lands before the ObjectDB leak dump, so the `Leaked instance:` lines that would tell you what leaked never print. On `gl_compatibility` the same project leaks the CanvasTexture and exits fine.

I have a fix for this and will open a PR.
### Steps to reproduce

1. New project, Node2D main scene, attach this script:

```gdscript
extends Node2D

var sprite: Sprite2D
var frames: int = 0

func _ready() -> void:
      var texture := CanvasTexture.new()
      texture.diffuse_texture = GradientTexture2D.new()
      sprite = Sprite2D.new()
      sprite.texture = texture
      sprite.position = Vector2(200, 200)
      add_child(sprite)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
      frames += 1
      if frames == 30:
              remove_child(sprite) # never freed, so it and its CanvasTexture leak
      if frames > 60:
              get_tree().quit()
```

2. Run it. The sprite has to be drawn before it's removed, since the callback is only registered while batching a CanvasTexture.
3. It quits itself after 60 frames and crashes with signal 11 on the way out.

Run it from the project directory and check the exit code: 134 on 4.4 and later, 0 on 4.3.

```sh
godot; echo $?
```

### Issue description

When using `camelCase`, `snake_case` or `kebab-case` options for `editor/naming/node_name_casing` project setting, and I add two nodes of same custom script class, the `NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED` notification fires two times on editor, the first one when the node is created and the second one when the name changes according to the project setting and (**should**) validate duplicate names, adding a number suffix.

When using the default value `PascalCase` (maybe should be renamed to `unchanged`, more on that later) and adding two nodes via the global script class name `Test`, I have the following output:

```
[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'Test'
'Test' entered tree

[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'Test2'
'Test2' entered tree
```

As expected, the second node receives the second new name with the correct suffix. But when using other name casing options, for example `snake_case`, it gives the following output:
```
[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'test'
'test' entered tree

[New Test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'Test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'Test' renamed to 'test'
'test2' entered tree
```

Notice how the number suffix is only added *after* the node is already added to the tree, and the second new name doesn't have the suffix.

Also, about the `PascalCase` default option for the project setting, it doesn't actually enforce the casing. For example, if by class is named `test`, I would expect the default option rename it to `Test`, but this isn't what happens, it simply leaves the name casing untouched.
```
[New test node]

'test' entered tree

[New test node]
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] '' renamed to 'test'
[NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED] 'test' renamed to 'test2'
'test2' entered tree
```

Notice how on the default value, the name casing is preserved, while adding the unique suffix before notifying NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED.

I used this script to test print:

```gdscript
@tool
class_name test extends Node

var previous_name: StringName = ""

func _init() -> void:
	print("[New test node]")

func _notification(what: int) -> void:
	if what == NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE:
		print("'%s' entered tree" % name)
	if what == NOTIFICATION_PATH_RENAMED:

		previous_name = name
```

### System information

Linux Arm64 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS in a Parallels VM on a macOS M5 Pro host

### Issue description

Compiling Godot with `scons target=template_release werror=yes` on Linux Arm64 gives the following dangling pointer warning:

```
In file included from modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:31:
In member function 'void GDScriptLanguage::enter_function(CallLevel*, GDScriptInstance*, GDScriptFunction*, Variant*, int*, int*)',
    inlined from 'Variant GDScriptFunction::call(GDScriptInstance*, const Variant**, int, Callable::CallError&, CallState*)' at modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:673:51:
modules/gdscript/gdscript.h:499:29: error: storing the address of local variable 'call_level' in 'GDScriptLanguage::_call_stack' [-Werror=dangling-pointer=]
  499 |                 _call_stack = call_level;
      |                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~
modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp: In member function 'Variant GDScriptFunction::call(GDScriptInstance*, const Variant**, int, Callable::CallError&, CallState*)':
modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:672:37: note: 'call_level' declared here
  672 |         GDScriptLanguage::CallLevel call_level;
      |                                     ^~~~~~~~~~
modules/gdscript/gdscript.h:433:40: note: 'GDScriptLanguage::_call_stack' declared here
  433 |         static thread_local CallLevel *_call_stack;
      |                                        ^~~~~~~~~~~
```



### Steps to reproduce

Attempt to compile a release template on Linux Arm64.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, it's the engine.
hints:
Technically it's a warning, not an error. It's only an error because you compile with `werror=yes`.

From the GDScript side, I'm confident in saying that this code is correct. The pointer gets cleaned up from that variable later in the function, without any possibilities for early returns. It's managed in a stack like fashion.

Should be trivial to suppress the warning in this case. If someone wants to do this, feel free to ping me for an approval.
patch:
diff --git a/modules/gdscript/gdscript.h b/modules/gdscript/gdscript.h
index 24bc684d35..c63f78c718 100644
--- a/modules/gdscript/gdscript.h
+++ b/modules/gdscript/gdscript.h
@@ -491,7 +491,17 @@ public:
 		}
 
 		call_level->prev = _call_stack;
+
+#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__) && __GNUC__ >= 12
+		GODOT_GCC_WARNING_PUSH_AND_IGNORE("-Wdangling-pointer") // The VM code ensures call_level is not freed while it is in use, so this warning is a false positive for GCC 12+.
+#endif
+
 		_call_stack = call_level;
+
+#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__) && __GNUC__ >= 12
+		GODOT_GCC_WARNING_POP
+#endif
+
 		call_level->stack = p_stack;
 		call_level->instance = p_instance;
 		call_level->function = p_function;

query:
OpenXR shutdown disconnects a nonexistent spatial discovery signal

### Tested versions

Reproducible in official builds:

- `4.7.1.stable.mono.official.a13da4feb`
- `4.7.dev5.mono.official.a8643700c`
- `4.6.2.stable.mono.official.71f334935`

Godot 4.2.2 did not complete the MRP within the bounded timeout and is below the tested project's API baseline, so it is not treated as a negative result.

### System information

Microsoft Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 (build 26200) - Godot 4.7.1 stable Mono - D3D12 12_0 (Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, driver 32.0.15.9579 - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X (32 threads) - SteamVR/OpenXR 2.16.7 - OpenXR 1.0.54

### Issue description

A standalone GDScript project initializes OpenXR through SteamVR, enables XR rendering for ten frames, disables XR on the viewport, calls `XRInterface.uninitialize()`, confirms `interface_initialized=false`, and exits with code 0.

At engine shutdown, Godot reports:

```text
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from '<OpenXRSpatialEntityExtension#...>'. Signal: 'spatial_discovery_recommended', callable: 'OpenXRSpatialMarkerTrackingCapability::_on_spatial_discovery_recommended'.
```

This reproduces when the OpenXR action map contains zero interaction profiles and the project does not use spatial entities. It also reproduces in a second cell containing one simple-controller profile.

Expected behavior: shutdown after explicit OpenXR teardown should not attempt to disconnect a signal connection that does not exist.

This is distinct from #113751, which concerned verbose orphan `StringName` diagnostics, and from #119042, where RID leaks followed a failed OpenXR session initialization. Here OpenXR initializes successfully and the application teardown completes before the diagnostic.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start SteamVR and select SteamVR as the active OpenXR runtime.
2. Download the MRP from `https://gist.github.com/zedarvates/bf1a9872453911f486473fc6ad85f904` and follow its README.
3. Run `run-probe.ps1` with the official Godot 4.7.1 Mono console executable and `-ExpectedOutcome reproduce`.
4. Observe that both cells report `initialized=True`, `teardown=True`, `timed_out=False`, and process exit 0.
5. Observe the nonexistent `spatial_discovery_recommended` signal disconnection after teardown in both full logs.
6. Run with `-ExpectedOutcome clean`; the runner exits with code 1 because the shutdown diagnostic remains.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://gist.github.com/zedarvates/bf1a9872453911f486473fc6ad85f904

The linked secret gist contains a base64-encoded ZIP with both GDScript projects, the bounded runner, instructions, and the two reference logs from Godot 4.7.1. The ZIP excludes `.godot`, C# code, addons, autoloads, and application assets.
hints:
Related: #122239 tracks the separate interaction-profile RID leak reproduced by the same minimal project.

Source diagnosis against the reported 4.7.1 commit: [on_session_created](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a13da4feb/modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_marker_tracking.cpp#L479-L488) returns before connecting when spatial_marker_tracking_ext is false, while [on_session_destroyed](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a13da4feb/modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_marker_tracking.cpp#L495-L515) reaches disconnect without the mirrored guard. Current master has the same asymmetry. This matches the MRP: SteamVR initializes, but the unavailable marker-tracking extension means no connection was created before teardown. A candidate fix is to mirror the extension guard or check is_connected before disconnecting. This is a source-level diagnosis; I have not runtime-tested a patched engine yet.

hints:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5773156e-370b-483c-9304-4b540ff1de85

I think this should fix it for single clicking. I didn't look into group selections or anything like that, but I'm not sure that's relevant with z-index issues.

> 2D selecting ignores `z_index`

It ignores rendering order in general. So all properties like `show_behind_parent`, `top_level`, `y_sort_enabled` are not taken into account as well. Same about containing canvas layers.

For all of them it's as trivial to create an example of "wrong selection" as for `z_index`.

Also note that `z_index` is considered separately for each rendering canvas; meaning a canvas item with greater `z_index` can still be drawn behind a canvas item with lower `z_index` (if they belong to different canvases, e.g. different CanvasLayer nodes).

Well my original problem was with TileMapLayer. I have a foreground layer and background layer and the back layer was being selected over the front one. It's rather annoying.

I looked into this and found it more complex than anticipated.

As covered, we have to look at several different attributes. Since I figured the `RenderingServer` was already doing all this, I looked there. The problem is, `RenderingServer` is all about setting information, not retrieving it. You `canvas_item_set_z_index()` and `canvas_item_set_sort_children_by_y()`, but you don't retrieve these values. It's one way, at least for the majority of `canvas_item` functions

For my PC, the `RenderingServer` seemed to be `RendererCanvasCull`  which calls `_render_canvas_item_tree()` which recursively calls `_cull_canvas_item()` which in turn uses `_attach_canvas_item_for_draw()` to add each `CanvasItem` to a list ready to be rendered.

The order in which they are added to the list (`z_list`) seems to be what determines the order that they're rendered in. The problem is that I don't know how to access this order. `RenderingServer` doesn't seem to have an API to access it.

Likewise, I don't know of any API that can, for instance, tell if one CanvasItem is in front of another. To see if I could find one, I did a search of `draw_behind_parent` but mostly only found the sections of code I've mentioned above.

So either we find a way to crack open the `RenderingServer`, or we recode all the functionality in a separate function, maybe one that sorts a small list of `CanvasItems`

There was a short discussion here about a bandaid solution:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/96584#issuecomment-2332307061

I'll try to double check tomorrow to see if the `RenderingServer` exposes any information regarding the absolute z order.

Besides the Godot editor, I imagine there are other usecases for knowing the renderered z order.

To me an API of some sort would make sense. Any issue with having the `RenderingServer` set a field in each node containing the proper sort order as rendered?

Some potential solutions

1. (As suggested) `RenderingServer` edits the `CanvasItem` to include their absolute z order. Feel unsure about this because it does it in secret
2. Edit `RenderingServer` API to include `canvas_item_sort_absolute_z` that takes a list of `CanvasItem` and sorts them front to back.
3. Edit `RenderingServer` API to include `canvas_item_get_frontmost` that takes a list of `CanvasItem` and returns the `CanvasItem` that's in front of all the others on that list.

I could potentially code up any of the above solutions, but since we're dealing with API that's used by more than one class and appears in documentation, I'd want some backup on which option to go for.

Created PR to fix this issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103365

I was in the process of making an issue report about this behavior as how it works now is simply **unintuitive** - especially in 2D scenes where a mix of 2D y-sorted nodes and different z-indexes are used, selecting the right node becomes a nightmare. Quick example video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e90d9cbe-9553-46e5-be59-0b102b9c4bc9

I checked how SelectResult order is implemented. It just uses CanvasItem's `z_index`, which uh, doesn't tell whether the node is on top or not. For a simple test, stack 2 sprites with `z_index` 5, and put another sprite with `z_index` of 6 as a sibling. The sibling sprite will appear behind the stacked one, but will get click priority.
And that's not even considering canvas layers or `top_level`.

For simple cases this issue can be considered fixed, but a more thorough fix might be needed eventually. Guess we'll see if users still run into this problem. And personally I even forgot I opened this issue xd It's not something I run into often.

CC @YeldhamDev

Well... My team and I are at least one of those users who run into this 1000 times a day, so if we already know the solution in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122510 isn't going to cut it, would it take a lot to improve on it?

I think `get_effective_z_index()` could be used here. I will work on that once I find the time.

iOS export fails to link: undefined symbols _SDL_IsIPad and _SDL_IsAppleTV in 4.7 templates

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.stable and 4.7.1.stable iOS export templates
- Not reproducible in 4.6.stable



### System information

macOS 15.7.7, Xcode 26.3 (17C529), iOS SDK 26.2, iPad Pro 11" (4th gen), Godot 4.7.1.stable, Mobile renderer

### Issue description

Linking an exported iOS project fails with two undefined symbols:
```
Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:
  "_SDL_IsIPad", referenced from: SDL.ios.template_debug.arm64.o in libgodot.a
  "_SDL_IsAppleTV", referenced from: SDL.ios.template_debug.arm64.o in libgodot.a
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
```

The `libgodot.a` shipped in the iOS template defines 869 SDL symbols, but not these two, they are the only SDL symbols in the archive left undefined. Upstream they live in `SDL_uikitvideo.m`, which isn't part of Godot's SDL build since only the joystick subsystem is compiled. Both the debug and release xcframeworks are affected.

This looks like it comes from #114316 (SDL3 joystick driver for iOS, merged for 4.7). CI builds the static library but never links an iOS app, linking only happens at export time, so the missing symbols pass CI.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Export any project for iOS with 4.7.1 templates, "Export Project Only"
2. Build for an arm64 device in Xcode
3. Linking fails with the symbols above

This can be confirmed without exporting anything, straight from the installed template:
```
nm libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/ios-arm64/libgodot.a | grep -c ' T _SDL_IsIPad'   # 0
nm -u libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/ios-arm64/libgodot.a | grep -c '_SDL_IsIPad'   # 1
```

Providing the two functions in the exported Xcode project makes it link, and the app runs on device with gamepad paths behaving normally:
```objective-c
#import <UIKit/UIKit.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

bool SDL_IsIPad(void)            { return UIDevice.currentDevice.userInterfaceIdiom == UIUserInterfaceIdiomPad; }
bool SDL_IsAppleTV(void)     { return false; }
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not needed, any project exported with the official 4.7.1 iOS templates reproduces it, and the `nm` check above confirms it on the shipped template alone.
hints:
I can't reproduce it, are you using modified Xcode project, or other libs / GDExtensions that are directly using SDL? While there symbols are indeed missing, ` SDL_IsTablet` and `SDL_IsTV` calling them are not used by the engine and should be optimized out.

No modified Xcode project, it's generated by the exporter with "Export Project Only" and built as-is. No GDExtensions, no native libraries in the project, and the three addons are pure GDScript. The only libraries linked are the ones the template ships.

I think the difference is the linker version. Build settings on my side:
```
XCODE_VERSION_ACTUAL = 2630 (Xcode 26.3)
DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING = YES
OTHER_LDFLAGS = (empty)
```

`OTHER_LDFLAGS` is `$(LD_CLASSIC_$(XCODE_VERSION_ACTUAL))`, and the generated project only defines `LD_CLASSIC_1500/1501/1510`, so on Xcode 26 it resolves to nothing and the modern linker is used. Dead stripping is on, yet the reference from `SDL_IsTablet/SDL_IsTV` still has to resolve at link time.

So it may only reproduce on Xcode 26.x.

> So it may only reproduce on Xcode 26.x.

I have tested it with Xcode 26.6 and 27.0 beta, and was not able to reproduce it on either.

I can reproduce this, but with `DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING` set to `NO` - the default is `YES`

Having the same issue on Xcode 26.6 with Godot 4.7.2.

Having the same issue for godot 4.8dev6 and Xcode 27

I did some more testing with full builds on Xcode 26.1.1, 26.3 and 26.6, with the Godot 4.7.1 and 4.7.2 templates. With the exported project's default settings it links fine, from both `xcodebuild` and the Xcode IDE.

I can recreate the issue only in the following scenarios:

- `DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=NO`
- `LD_EXPORT_GLOBAL_SYMBOLS=YES` - adds `-rdynamic`, so it fails even with dead stripping on
- `ENABLE_TESTABILITY=YES` - also passes `-rdynamic` to the linker ([Apple docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/build-settings-reference#Enable-Testability))

The exported Xcode project has all three off.

New Xcode projects have `ENABLE_TESTABILITY=YES` in Debug by default (set in Xcode's base project template `Library/Xcode/Templates/Project Templates/Base/Base_ProjectSettings.xctemplate/TemplateInfo.plist`), so it might be encountered if the export's settings have been changed or it's been added to another project.

Would someone who can reproduce this be able to provide the full link command that Xcode runs? This is in the Report navigator (<kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>9</kbd>): select the failed build, expand the "Link output" step and copy the command. It will show whether `-dead_strip` is missing or `-rdynamic` is present.

The problem is that an animation track is a function over time, so $f(t) = y$ is your animated value for a given time $t$. Here, you've got multiple keyframes at the same point in time (time 1 is time 0 in the next iteration of the loop), so both $f(0) = f(1) = y_1$ and $f(0) = f(1) = y_2$ need to be true (for $y_1 \ne y_2$). That previous fix accounted for the user expectation that $f(0) \ne f(1)$ must be possible by replacing $f$ with a new function $g$, so that

$$
g(t) = \begin{cases}
    f(t - \epsilon) & \text{if } t = 1 \\
    f(t) & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

That works for linear interpolation, because the singularity at $t = 1$ only affects that particular $t$, so the problem can be hidden by just preventing the user from looking there. With cubic interpolation, however, $f(t)$ is influenced by four different keyframes, so with only two keyframes in the animation (both of which will be used twice to get to the four keyframes required), the function is now undefined on the entire length of the animation. Internally, this leads to a number of division by zeros that the algorithm gracefully handles by just returning "something" when it encounters zero-length segments. This prevents crashes, but the result is rather arbitrary and won't magically produce a function that can be in two places at once.

Enabling "Clamp" actually makes the function discontinuous at $t = 1$, so while $t = 0$ and $t = 1$ still refer to the same position in the loop, $f$ may now indeed have two different values at the loop point. The cubic interpolation will then see that there is no way to reach four keyframes along the time axis and fall back to linear interpolation, which most likely matches what users would expect should happen in this case.

_Edit:_ Since it may be hard to visualize what actually happens here, I've plotted a few examples of animation track interpolation (click to enlarge):
![grafik](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/35597337/6b40e4e6-c829-45ee-be92-7b5d7b638117)

The left column shows linear interpolation, the right column cubic interpolation. All animations are defined on a 0-1 time range and four runs through the loop are shown. There's always a keyframe at (0, 0) and a second keyframe at (0.5, 1), (0.9, 1) and (1, 1) going down the rows.

You can see that with linear interpolation, the only real difference between a second keyframe at (0.9, 1) and at (1, 1) is that the curve becomes discontinuous (there is no vertical green line) in the latter case, i. e. there is no problem outside of those very specific points.

For cubic, on the other hand, the curve looks as expected with a second keyframe at (0,5, 1) and (0.9, 1), but transforms into an entirely different shape that even runs backwards most most of the way with the keyframe at (1, 1). The curve is mathematically undefined at this point, so you can't blame the algorithm for just doodling a bit.

Actually, even the cubic 0.9 case may not quite be "as expected" if you're thinking of easing. "Cubic interpolation" computes a cubic spline through the keyframes and if they're close together, this spline will go far outside the convex hull of the keyframes. If instead you're just looking for some non-linearity in your interpolation, stick to linear interpolation and set the "Easing" value in the properties of the keyframe to something other than 1.0.

I may have put a bit too much effort into explaining why I think what happens is technically correct, while the real issue should probably be: What is the user trying to achieve and how can Godot make it easy to find the right tools for the job and explain what the effects of the individual options are.

That observation for the different behavior in 3.5.2 is very interesting. I'm no expert on the animation system but I had a quick glance at the code and there is indeed a difference here in that 3.5.2 doesn't even take the time of the two outer keyframes into consideration, so short time intervals can't ever be an issue here. The definition of "cubic interpolation" changed between 3.5 and 4 and I'd assume that the 3.5 approach was much less prone to overswings. That change was made in #63602 and I think the idea was that this makes the resulting curve smoother, even though it may overshoot the keyframes. The PR has an animation where the overshoots indeed look quite natural.

So I suppose that's just how cubic interpolation works in Godot 4 now. And I see how for many 2D animations, you might have preferred the old way. Still, I think you should often be able to get a similar effect as before by using linear interpolation with easing.

Not dealing with the two outer keys in the wrap loop is a cubic completion in Godot 3.x is obviously wrong behavior.

If there is no key overlap, then the Godot4 behavior is correct and the 3.x behavior is clearly wrong . The problem is ambiguity in Godot4 in getting the key when the keys overlap (quite a special case). If you just want to emulate godot 3.x behavior, just use clamp mode.

> 3.5 approach was much less prone to overswings. That change was made in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63602 and I think the idea was that this makes the resulting curve smoother, even though it may overshoot the keyframes. The PR has an animation where the overshoots indeed look quite natural.

#63602 has nothing related to the overshooting issue. It simply corrects the wrong cubic interpolation since it does not take into account the interval between keys. To solve the overshooting problem, it is necessary to adopt makima interpolation, etc. as described in #57952.

What I meant by "3.5 was less prone to overswings" was that for Godot 4, #63602 replaced the previous `_cubic_interpolate` with `_cubic_interpolate_in_time`, which produces a curve that for non-regular keyframe intervals is much smoother but no longer restricted to the value range of the keyframes:
![grafik](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/35597337/042df12c-717d-4feb-8590-bbb8c66dc225)

I'm not saying that's wrong, I just brought that up to clear up any misconceptions and explain the different behavior between Godot 3.5 and Godot 4. I can understand why a user less familiar with polynomial interpolation, who might think of cubic interpolation as "just like linear, but smoother" and would use it to interpolate typical 2D things like color fades, sliding doors, or opening menus, might be surprised that, for example, the animation can go well into the negatives even without a single negative keyframe. In most audio or video editing software that I know and that has 2D curves for volume, compositing levels, and the like, they usually offer quadratic, cubic, exponential etc. easing in/easing out modes per keyframe, but no interpolation across more than two keyframes:

![grafik](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/35597337/02cb52d8-eebd-4fbf-b78d-7377385103f6)

Since the terms are similar, I can see why people may initially insist on using cubic interpolation in Godot even if it's not what they think of and detrimental to what they want to achieve. If you're making something like a path, however, and smoothness is your main priority and you don't want your spaceship to stop at every waypoint, then this corrected cubic interpolation is of course superior to any kind of linear interpolation with easing.

If you're making something like a path, however, and smoothness is your main priority and you don't want your spaceship to stop at every waypoint, then this corrected cubic interpolation is of course superior to any kind of linear interpolation with easing.

Just because it looks different from the previous motion and from the behavior in other animation programs - it's a bit confusing. It's clear to me that there are many options to use the current behavior as more natural, I just don't have to deal with it in my tasks. It seems like it would be useful to just have both options for different situations.

Different programs use different animation interface designs, so it's always just a matter of getting used to it. For example, easing in Godot was quite strange to me, because it only customizes the ease_out of frame, as well as separating tracks into two types: curves and values, when they are essentially the same thing. Nevertheless the animation editor in Godot allows you to do all necessary things its own special way. A universal interface for all purposes is quite a challenge, I understand that. iOS: "Mouse is not supported by this display server." error on every startup

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable

### System information

iOS 26.6.2 (iPhone 12 Pro, Apple A14) - Godot v4.7.2.stable.official - Metal 4.0 - Forward Mobile; exported from macOS 26.6 with Xcode 27.0

### Issue description

On iOS, every app launch prints this error once, even for an empty project (not tested on Android yet) :

```
ERROR: Mouse is not supported by this display server.
   at: mouse_get_position (servers/display/display_server.cpp:536)
```

It comes from the root Window entering the tree. Window::_notification() (scene/main/window.cpp, NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE, root window branch) simulates a mouse-enter event:

```
// Simulate mouse-enter event when mouse is over the window, since OS event might arrive before setting callbacks.
if (!mouse_in_window && Rect2(position, size).has_point(DisplayServer::get_singleton()->mouse_get_position())) {
```

mouse_get_position() is called without checking FEATURE_MOUSE, unlike Viewport::get_mouse_position(), which checks it and falls back to Input.

The app works fine, but the error is noisy: crash reporting tools that forward engine errors (I use Sentry) record an error event for every launch.

Expected: no error on display servers without mouse support.

1. Open the attached MRP (empty scene, file logging enabled so the error is visible without a debugger).
2. Add an iOS export preset with your signing settings and export/run it on an iOS device.
3. Read user://logs/godot.log from the app's Documents folder (or watch the Xcode console): the error above is printed right after startup.

query: Inspector dock's "Show in FileSystem" can be invoked via its shortcut while showing as disabled, crashing with an ERR_FAIL_COND ### Tested versions Reproducible in: 4.8.dev (e16296832) I have not tested other versions in this session, but this is very unlikely to be a recent regression: `InspectorDock::_get_current_resource()` (the function the crashing code path relies on) has only ever cast the currently inspected object to `Resource`, with no history of ever handling a plain `Node`, and the popup's disabled-state refresh timing described below has been the same since this dock's "resource extra" popup was introduced. I could not find any commit that changed this behavior. ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (e16296832) - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (12 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The Inspector dock has a "resource extra" `MenuButton` popup (New Resource / Load Resource / Save / Save As / Edit Resource from Clipboard / Copy Resource / **Show in FileSystem** / Open Documentation / Make Resource Built-In), with several of its items also bound to a user-assignable keyboard shortcut (none of them ship with a default keybinding). When the object currently shown in the Inspector is a **Node** rather than a **Resource** (for example, a node that is itself the root of an externally instantiated scene), the "Show in FileSystem" item is correctly shown as disabled if you actually open this popup. However, pressing its assigned shortcut *without* first opening the popup for this selection still runs the action, and it crashes with: ``` ERROR: Condition "current_res.is_null()" is true. at: _menu_option_confirm (editor/docks/inspector_dock.cpp:108) ``` Root cause: `MenuButton::shortcut_input()` dispatches to `PopupMenu::activate_item_by_event()`, which does correctly check `is_item_disabled()` before running the bound action -- but only against whatever disabled-state was last written to that specific item. Most of this popup's items (Save, Save As, Copy Resource, Make Resource Built-In, Open Documentation) have their disabled-state recomputed on every Inspector selection change (`InspectorDock::update()`). "Show in FileSystem" (and "Edit Resource from Clipboard") are the exception: their disabled-state is only recomputed when the popup is actually opened (`_prepare_resource_extra_popup()`, connected to the button's `about_to_popup` signal). So a pure keyboard shortcut press, without ever opening the popup for the current selection, can activate "Show in FileSystem" while it's actually invalid for the current selection -- its item never had a chance to be marked disabled in the first place. Expected behavior: pressing the shortcut while the current object has no corresponding non-built-in `Resource` to show should simply do nothing (matching what the menu item's own disabled appearance already implies), not crash with an `ERR_FAIL_COND`. I have a small, local fix ready (a single predicate, `_is_menu_option_enabled()`, used both to compute every item's disabled-state -- now refreshed uniformly and consistently for the whole popup -- and as an early-return guard at the top of `_menu_option_confirm()`, so a menu option can never actually run while invalid regardless of what any `PopupMenu` item's disabled flag happens to say at the moment) and will follow up with a pull request shortly after opening this issue. Before (selecting a Node in the Inspector, then pressing the Inspector's "Show in FileSystem" shortcut without opening the popup first -- crashes with the error above): After (with the fix applied, the same key press is a silent no-op, matching the item's own disabled state -- no error, no crash): ### Steps to reproduce 1. In Editor Settings -> Shortcuts, search for "Show in FileSystem" and assign a key combination to the **Property Editor** entry specifically (it has no default keybinding). 2. In any project, select any **Node** in a scene (any node at all -- it does not need to be an instantiated sub-scene; a plain `Node3D` reproduces this too) so the Inspector shows its properties. 3. Without opening the Inspector's "resource extra" popup (the small button with the dropdown next to the object path, at the top of the Inspector) even once for this selection, press the shortcut assigned in step 1. Expected: nothing happens -- no change in the FileSystem dock, no console output. Actual: this is printed to the console, and nothing else happens: ``` ERROR: Condition "current_res.is_null()" is true. at: _menu_option_confirm (editor/docks/inspector_dock.cpp:108) ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A -- any project works, as long as it contains at least one Node to select in a scene (see step 2 above). No special project setup is required to reproduce this.

query:
Godot crashes when clearing non 16 aligned gpu buffers

### Tested versions

master, but also reproduced in earlier 4.x versions. I initially discovered this while working on a project with the latests 4.7 stable release

### System information

win 10, forward+/mobile, dx12, gtx5080

### Issue description

When calling buffer_clear with a p_offset that is not a multiple of 16 the DX12 rendering driver just crashes. On vulkan anything that is a multiple of 4 works fine.

According to git blame the code responsible for this bug has existed for at least for 10 months already.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the project, ensure it is using DX12 and run the scene.
If the renderer is switched to vulkan or the offset parameter of the script is changed to 16 the game should stop crashing and print a success message to the console.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)


[buffer_clear.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32533711/buffer_clear.zip)
hints:
Running the MRP with `--gpu-validation` and using DebugView, i get the following errors before the crash: ``` D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12Device::CreateUnorderedAccessView: When creating a RAW Shader Resource View, the offset of the first element from the start of the buffer must be a multiple of 16 bytes. Thus, FirstElement (1) must be a multiple of 4 since each element is 4 bytes. [ STATE_CREATION ERROR #345: CREATEUNORDEREDACCESSVIEW_INVALIDDIMENSIONS] D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12Device::RemoveDevice: Device removal has been triggered for the following reason (DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL: There is strong evidence that the application has performed an illegal or undefined operation, and such a condition could not be returned to the application cleanly through a return code). [ EXECUTION ERROR #232: DEVICE_REMOVAL_PROCESS_AT_FAULT] D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandList::ClearUnorderedAccessViewUint: The CPU and GPU descriptor handles refer to unmatched descriptors. ClearUnorderedAccessView* methods require that the GPU and CPU descriptor handles reside in separate shader-visible and non-shader-visible descriptor heaps resptively. These descriptors must otherwise be identical. [ EXECUTION ERROR #646: INVALID_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE] D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandList::ClearUnorderedAccessViewUint: Descriptor (at CPU Handle 0x000002003432C180) which has an underlying stale or released resource is invalid for use. [ EXECUTION ERROR #1042: DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE_WITH_INVALID_RESOURCE] ```
From the first two errors seems that's how D3D12 operates, so the offset needs to follow the 16 bytes alignment. Would be good if we could add a check to handle it more gracefully if possible. Pinging @blueskythlikesclouds to see if there's something that can be done about it. Ah, I posted this in rc on the rendering channel, but apparently didn't mention it here. I have little experience working with dx12 (more used to OpenGL and Vulkan) but looking at the docs I suspect we could have an UAV that is 16 aligned and then use the optional rect Parameter of the clear command to only clear what we actually want to clear. However, I would like to get confirmation from someone who is more familiar with DX that doing so won't have any unintended side effects or cause a performance regression before I try to throw together a PR.

### Issue description

Under specific circumstances, trying to assign a C# Resource (class created and used in C#) from GDScript will give the `Cannot assign a new value to a constant.` error.
For this error to happen, the C# class must inherit from `Resource` (`RefCounted`, `GodotObject` and `Node` don't give this error), must have the `[GlobalClass]` attribute, and when defined in another class, must have `[Export]`

This is honestly really confusing to describe, so I'll just give a small code example:
```cs
// res://MyResource.cs
[GlobalClass] // Must be a [GlobalClass] for the error to happen
public partial class MyResource : Resource { } // Must be a Resource for the error to happen

// res://MyOtherClass.cs
[GlobalClass]
public partial class MyOtherClass : Node // The type this class inherits from doesn't matter
{
    [Export] public MyResource MyRes; // Must have [Export] for the error to happen
}
```
```gdscript
extends Node
func _ready():
   var test := MyOtherClass.new()
   test.MyRes = null # Cannot assign a new value to a constant.
   test.MyRes = MyResource.new() # Cannot assign a new value to a constant.
```

### Steps to reproduce

I've kind of describe them above, and I've also included an MRP below, which should hopefully clear things up more.
When making a change to the C# side of the MRP, don't forget to re-compile and to save the GDScript script again.
Sometimes, the script editor might not update properly and won't show the error, but the Output tab will always have the error if it's there. You can always save the script to make the error show up in the Output tab.

### Issue description

The editor's 3d viewport camera exhibits incorrect panning behaviour, snapping back to previous positions even when it clearly shouldn't, or at the very least without the user intending it to.

3. while holding the middle mouse button, move the mouse around to pan

5. without moving the mouse even a single pixel, release the middle mouse button
6. without moving the mouse even a single pixel, press and hold the right mouse button
7. observe that the camera has now incorrectly snapped back to the position before the middle-mouse pan, and the right mouse button pan is now completely ignored by the editor and won't move the camera at all

In `RenderForwardMobile::_render_particle_collider_heightfield()` (`servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp`) the heightfield depth pass is drawn with `_render_list_with_draw_list(&render_list_params, p_fb);` i.e. with the default draw flags, so the heightfield depth texture is **loaded** instead of cleared. Forward+ passes `RD::DRAW_CLEAR_ALL` in the same place, and 4.3 Mobile used `INITIAL_ACTION_CLEAR` (lost in the DrawFlags refactor). Consequences: - The depth test keeps the highest value, so every update only *adds* to the old contents. A heightfield that is moved (follow camera, or simply repositioned, including in the editor) becomes a "solid block" at the highest height it has ever seen — which matches the 4.6.dev4 Windows/Vulkan report above. - A freshly created heightfield texture starts with whatever was in that memory: it is not cleared on creation on Vulkan (only D3D12 sets `API_TRAIT_TEXTURE_OUTPUTS_REQUIRE_CLEARS`), so depending on the driver/allocator you can get no collision at all or garbage. Reproduced on 4.7.2.stable / Windows 11 / Vulkan / NVIDIA, with MSAA disabled (the heightfield framebuffer is single-sampled anyway, so depth resolve should not be involved). Passing `RD::DRAW_CLEAR_ALL` there (the Mobile `_render_list_with_draw_list` already defaults the depth clear value to 0.0 = far with reversed-Z) should fix it. One more data point: this was already fixed once for 4.4 in #102133 ("Fix framebuffer clear for particle collider heightfield", fixes #100793) — but that one-line patch only touched `render_forward_clustered.cpp`. The Mobile counterpart in `render_forward_mobile.cpp` never got the `RD::DRAW_CLEAR_ALL`, so Mobile still has the bug that Forward+ had in 4.4dev6/dev7. Details and a repro in #124252.

query:
Compatibility: SSAO forces an unused per-frame MSAA depth+stencil copy into the 3D back buffer (several ms per frame on ANGLE/D3D11)

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (web export with the official templates, and desktop with `--rendering-driver opengl3_angle`).
- The code paths below are unchanged on `master` (65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704).

### System information

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26340), Godot v4.7.2.stable - Compatibility - Chrome 154.0.8037.98, WebGL 2: `ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (0x00002882) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)`. Desktop native GL: NVIDIA 610.88.

### Issue description

In the Compatibility renderer, enabling SSAO makes every frame copy the **multisampled** main depth+stencil buffer into the 3D back-buffer depth texture, but nothing reads that copy. Under ANGLE/D3D11 (Chrome and Edge on Windows, and `opengl3_angle` on desktop) the multisampled stencil resolve is very slow, so SSAO costs several milliseconds per frame that have nothing to do with SSAO itself.

The chain, per frame:

1. [`rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2771-L2773`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2771-L2773): `if (ssao_enabled) scene_state.used_depth_texture = true;`
2. [`#L2951-L2952`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2951-L2952): that calls `rb->check_backbuffer(...)`, which ends in an unconditional `glCheckFramebufferStatus` even when nothing was (re)created ([`render_scene_buffers_gles3.cpp#L552`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/storage/render_scene_buffers_gles3.cpp#L552)).
3. [`#L2974-L2976`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2974-L2976): `glBlitFramebuffer(..., GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT | GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT, GL_NEAREST)` from the MSAA fbo into the back-buffer depth texture.

But SSAO is applied in `post_copy`, which reads the internal (resolved) depth, not the back-buffer depth ([`#L3124`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L3124)). With no material using `hint_depth_texture`, the copy is dead work. For comparison, Godot's own MSAA resolve later in the same frame blits `COLOR|DEPTH` (0x4100) without stencil.

**Measured with the MRP below** (web release export, Chrome with vsync and the frame rate limit off, 3 alternating rounds, 944x445 canvas):

| Variant | Mean fps | Frame ms |
|---|---|---|
| a. SSAO on, MSAA 4x | 258 | 3.88 |
| b. SSAO off, MSAA 4x | 667 | 1.50 |
| c. SSAO on, stencil bit removed from that one blit (JS shim) | 636 | 1.57 |
| d. SSAO on, MSAA off | 626 | 1.60 |
| e. SSAO on, `glCheckFramebufferStatus` faked, blit kept | 311 | 3.21 |
| f. SSAO on, that blit skipped entirely | 657 | 1.52 |

At 1904x985: a = 97 fps (10.3 ms), b = 481, c = 478, f = 467. So the cost grows with resolution, about 8 ms per frame at 1080p.

- The cost is the multisampled **stencil** resolve. Dropping only the stencil bit (c), or skipping the copy (f), recovers almost everything. Faking the framebuffer check alone (e) does not: the stall then surfaces at the next sync point.
- Single-sampled depth+stencil blits are cheap (d).
- The picture does not change. Screenshots of a vs c and a vs f differ in **0 pixels** (fps label cropped). b differs from a in 188k pixels, so SSAO is visibly active.
- Desktop, 960x540, same project: `opengl3_angle` gives ~285 fps with SSAO on vs ~855 with it off. Native `opengl3` on NVIDIA shows no measurable difference, so this mainly hits ANGLE (that is, most web players on Windows).

We first saw it in a real game's web build: about 5 ms per frame (48.8 to 65.4 fps with the stencil bit removed, 74.3 with SSAO off).

**Possible fixes** (any one helps, the first is the largest):

1. Don't force `used_depth_texture` for SSAO, since post reads the internal depth.
2. When the back-buffer depth copy *is* needed (`hint_depth_texture`), blit `GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT` only. The texture is only ever sampled as depth.
3. In `check_backbuffer`, call `glCheckFramebufferStatus` only when an attachment was (re)created. This one alone is small, about 0.5 ms here.

Workaround for affected web projects: a small JS hook on `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.blitFramebuffer` that clears `STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT` when the read framebuffer's depth-stencil attachment is a multisampled renderbuffer and the draw framebuffer's is a texture.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP and export it for Web (single-threaded), or run it on desktop with `--rendering-driver opengl3_angle`.

```gdscript
extends Node3D
# Runtime switches, polled once a second so one page load serves every variant:
#   web:     location.hash, e.g. index.html#ssao=0&msaa=0
#   desktop: user args,     e.g. godot --path . -- ssao=0 msaa=0
@onready var env: Environment = $WorldEnvironment.environment
var _opts := "?"
var _t := 1.0

func _ready() -> void:
	$Camera3D.look_at_from_position(Vector3(0, 9, 12), Vector3.ZERO)
	$Sun.rotation_degrees = Vector3(-50, 30, 0)
	var ground := MeshInstance3D.new()
	ground.mesh = PlaneMesh.new()
	ground.mesh.size = Vector2(40, 40)
	add_child(ground)

		m.mesh = BoxMesh.new() if i % 2 == 0 else SphereMesh.new()
		m.position = Vector3(i % 8 - 3.5, 0.5 + (i % 3) * 0.4, floori(i / 8.0) - 3.5) * 1.4
		add_child(m)
	RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time(get_viewport().get_viewport_rid(), true)

func _read_opts() -> String:
	if OS.has_feature("web"):
		return str(JavaScriptBridge.eval("location.hash"))
	return " ".join(OS.get_cmdline_user_args())

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	_t += delta
	if _t < 1.0:
		return
	_t = 0.0
	var opts := _read_opts()
	if opts != _opts:
		_opts = opts
		env.ssao_enabled = not opts.contains("ssao=0")
		get_viewport().msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_DISABLED if opts.contains("msaa=0") else Viewport.MSAA_4X
	var vp := get_viewport().get_viewport_rid()
	var line := "fps %d ssao=%s msaa=%d cpu_ms=%.2f gpu_ms=%.2f" % [Engine.get_frames_per_second(),
		env.ssao_enabled, get_viewport().msaa_3d, RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu(vp),
		RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu(vp)]
	$Label.text = line
	print(line)
```
