Metal: push constants re-applied by compute_list_add_barrier() overwrite the next pipeline's uniform set (GPU page fault, timeout waiting for fence freeze)

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.dev7.official [c971f93e7]
- Not tested, but the same code path exists in 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable and current master (e7cfa294a0). See "Cause" below.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Unknown (27.0.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

On Metal, if `compute_list_add_barrier()` is followed by a dispatch of a pipeline that has **no** push constants, that pipeline's uniform set gets overwritten. The overwrite happens at the Metal buffer index where the *previous* pipeline kept its push constants. The other drivers are not affected, because push constants there do not share slots with descriptor sets.

In the MRP this only produces a wrong result. In a real project the overwritten set held 20 sampled textures (a 320-byte argument buffer). The shader then read texture handles out of the 16 bytes of push constant data, which caused `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`. After that, Metal ignores every further command buffer (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored`), and the engine freezes with an endless stream of:

```
ERROR: timeout waiting for fence
   at: wait (drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal3.cpp:58)
```

The freeze happened at random, but the overwrite happened on every frame.

#### Cause

1. `RenderingDevice::compute_list_add_barrier()` ends the compute list, begins a new one, and re-records the previous pipeline, uniform sets **and push constants** ([rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216)).
2. During replay, `MDCommandBufferBase::encode_push_constant_data()` stores the data, sets `push_constant_binding` to the push constant index of the *previous* shader (index 1 here, because that shader only has set 0), and sets `DIRTY_PUSH` ([metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728)).
3. The caller binds a different pipeline. `MDCommandBuffer::bind_pipeline()` marks the pipeline and the uniform sets dirty, but leaves `DIRTY_PUSH` and `push_constant_binding` untouched ([metal3_objects.cpp#L431-L437](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L431-L437)).
4. On dispatch, `_compute_set_dirty_state()` first binds the new uniform sets (set 1 goes to buffer index 1). It then still sees `DIRTY_PUSH` and calls `setBytes(push_constant_data, 16, push_constant_binding = 1)`, which overwrites set 1 ([metal3_objects.cpp#L1616-L1639](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L1616-L1639)).

If the next pipeline has push constants of its own, they replace the stale ones before the dispatch. That is why only push-constant-less pipelines are affected.

#### Possible fix

When `bind_pipeline()` switches to a pipeline with a different shader, drop any pending push constants: clear `DIRTY_PUSH` and reset `push_constant_binding`. This matches the RD contract, because `RenderingDevice` already requires push constants to be supplied again after a shader change (`pipeline_push_constant_supplied = false`, [rendering_device.cpp#L6852-L6856](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L6852-L6856)). The render branch of `bind_pipeline()` and `_render_set_dirty_state()` have the same structure.

#### Workaround

Before a dispatch without push constants, end the compute list and begin a new one instead of calling `compute_list_add_barrier()`.

Possibly related: #119436 (same freeze symptom, but the trigger there appears to be long-running compute work).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached MRP on a Mac with the Metal driver.
2. Run the main scene. Expected output: `OK` twice. Actual output:
   ```
   Separate compute lists: OK (1234)
   compute_list_add_barrier: WRONG (0, expected 1234)
   ```
3. Optional: run with `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_ERROR_MODE=nslog`. Metal then reports that buffer slot 1 holds the 16-byte push constant block instead of set 1:
   ```
   Compute Function(main0): argument spvDescriptorSet1[0] from Buffer(1) with offset(0) and length(16) has space for 16 bytes, but argument has a length(24).
   ```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The MRP dispatches a producer (set 0 + 16-byte push constant) and then a consumer (set 0 + set 1, no push constants) in one compute list. Between them it either calls `compute_list_add_barrier()` or ends the list and begins a new one.

query:
`SceneTree` accessibility change queue grows forever without screen reader support (headless / no AccessKit)

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5-stable and later (tested 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable), current `master` (4.8-dev) has the same code.
- Not reproducible in: 4.4.1-stable (no accessibility API yet).

All builds are from source without the AccessKit dependencies (the build prints "The screen reader support driver requires dependencies to be installed").

### System information

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.9), AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 8840HS. Reproduced with `--headless` and with the X11 display server; our target is Linux.

### Issue description

`SceneTree::accessibility_change_queue` (`HashSet<ObjectID>`) grows forever when the display server has no screen reader support (headless, or any build without AccessKit). Every GUI node that has ever been in the tree keeps its id in the set, including nodes that were freed long ago. Object count stays flat, only static memory grows.

Why:

- `Node::queue_accessibility_update()` inserts the node id unconditionally. `Control` calls it on entering the tree and on size changes, and so do `Label`, `Button`, containers and other GUI classes.
- The queue is consumed only by `_flush_accessibility_changes()` -> `_process_accessibility_changes()`, which runs only when `is_accessibility_enabled()` is true.
- On `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` the id is erased only when `is_accessibility_supported()` is true (`scene/main/node.cpp`).

Without screen reader support neither path runs, so nothing is ever removed.

The code was added in b106dfd4f9 "Base accessibility API." (#76829) and is unchanged on `master`.

Impact: in our UI-heavy app every scene change adds about 20–35 KB, and screens that create GUI nodes at runtime add more on top. An application that runs for weeks without a restart and changes scenes regularly keeps growing.

Possible fix: skip the insert in `SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change()` when `!is_accessibility_supported()` (nothing will ever process those entries), or do the same check in `Node::queue_accessibility_update()`.

```diff
--- a/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
+++ b/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
@@ -243,7 +243,7 @@ void SceneTree::_accessibility_notify_change(const Node *p_node, bool p_remove)
 	if (p_node) {
 		if (p_remove) {
 			accessibility_change_queue.erase(p_node->get_instance_id());
-		} else {
```

query:
Metal: RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED underflows when textures are freed

### Tested versions

Tested versions: reproducible in 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf] and in master [c9730f40a] built locally. Not reproducible with --rendering-driver vulkan (MoltenVK) on the same machine.

### System information

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.3), Apple M4, Metal 4.0, Forward+.

### Issue description

The following is my (mostly Claude's) understanding of the issue.

Our stream's OpenTelemetry gauge for Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED read about 9.2e18. That's int() clamping the float the monitor returns, which is about 1.8e19, i.e. the uint64 counter wrapped below zero. A bare project with no game code reproduces it.

- Root cause:
  - RenderingDevice adds texture_get_allocation_size() to its counter only for textures it allocates (in texture_create and shared fallbacks). On free, it subtracts that size for every texture (_free_pending_resources).
  - Every 2D texture also gets an sRGB view (rd_texture_srgb, created by texture_create_shared in texture_storage.cpp).
  - Vulkan returns 0 for a view because it empties the view's allocation.
  - Metal returns the view's MTLTexture.allocatedSize, which is the parent's size, so each texture is subtracted twice.
  - Textures imported with texture_create_from_extension have the same asymmetry: never added, but subtracted on Metal.
- Fix: in drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.cpp, texture_get_allocation_size returns 0 for views (parentTexture() != nullptr) and for imported textures, as Vulkan does. It's 2 lines.
- Side effect: with the fix, the counter's starting value is higher (about 4.8 MB vs 2.67 MB), because views freed during startup no longer get subtracted. The new number is the accurate one.
- Not tested: the imported-texture case. It needs a GDExtension or XR texture

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on macOS with Godot 4.7.2 or master, using the Metal driver (the project sets rendering_device/driver.macos="metal", Forward+).
2. Run it. It waits 10 frames, creates 20 RGBA8 256×256 ImageTextures (5,242,880 bytes in all), frees them 10 frames later, prints Performance.RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED at each step, then quits. A helper in the script prints a wrapped counter as a negative number, so the drop is easy to read.
3. Look at the output. Creating adds about 5,242,880 bytes, but freeing takes off about 10,485,000, roughly twice that. The counter ends up below where it started and wraps around (it reads as about 1.8e19 without the helper).
4. For comparison, run the same project with --rendering-driver vulkan. Freeing then takes off exactly what creating added.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[metal-texture-mem-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33347162/metal-texture-mem-mrp.zip)
hints:
> The following is my (mostly Claude's) understanding of the issue.

Please see [this](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#for-contributors), if you are using AI tools to assist in investigating issues please make sure to verify any AI output before pasting it

Also reproduces on master d824ca9fe2, M1 on macOS 26.2.

The imported texture case can be checked without a GDExtension by importing the native handle of a texture you just made. For a 256x256 RGBA8 texture, creating and freeing a shared view or an imported copy each takes 264192 off the counter on Metal, and nothing on Vulkan:

```
metal
texture_create: +264192
shared view, created and freed: -264192
texture_create_from_extension, created and freed: -264192
total after freeing everything: -528384

vulkan
texture_create: +264192
shared view, created and freed: +0
texture_create_from_extension, created and freed: +0
total after freeing everything: +0
```

To reproduce the imported case:
```gdscript
var rd := RenderingServer.get_rendering_device()
var fmt := RDTextureFormat.new()
fmt.width = 256
fmt.height = 256
fmt.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM
fmt.usage_bits = RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_SAMPLING_BIT | RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_UPDATE_BIT
var texture := rd.texture_create(fmt, RDTextureView.new())
var handle := rd.get_driver_resource(RenderingDevice.DRIVER_RESOURCE_TEXTURE, texture, 0)
var before := rd.get_memory_usage(RenderingDevice.MEMORY_TEXTURES)
var imported := rd.texture_create_from_extension(RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D, fmt.format,
		RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_SAMPLES_1, fmt.usage_bits, handle, 256, 256, 1, 1)
rd.free_rid(imported)
# frees are deferred, so wait a few frames, then compare get_memory_usage() with `before`
```

Looking into it it seems a wayland surface is getting destroyed in between the activation token being created and used. I'm working on it.
edit: I think I found the bug. It's a concurrency use after free that was never a problem before. @deralmas I see two options:

multimesh_allocate_data with use_indirect does not initialize command buffer

### Tested versions

4.5 stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9159) - AMD Ryzen 5 5500 (12 threads) - 31.87 GiB memory

### Issue description

After calling `multimesh_allocate_data` on a multimesh, the command_buffer is not initialized until the next call to multimesh_set_mesh.
This can be confirmed in current master [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L1580) where the command buffer is reset to null, and only initialized [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L1690) when multimesh_set_mesh is called.

This is understandable when mesh is null, because the command buffer requires information on vertex / index count. However when the mesh is already set, it may be expected for the command buffer to be initialized automatically.

Otherwise, if this is the expected behavior, the docs for [multimesh_allocate_data](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-allocate-data) should probably be updated to reflect this information as the current one is empty; while the docs for [multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-get-command-buffer-rd-rid) only mentions the following:

> This [RID](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_rid.html#class-rid) is only valid if use_indirect is set to true when allocating data through [multimesh_allocate_data()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-allocate-data)

which could possibly be confusing.




### Steps to reproduce

run the following in a blank scene

```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var mm = RenderingServer.multimesh_create()
	var mesh = BoxMesh.new()
	RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh(mm, mesh.get_rid())
	RenderingServer.multimesh_allocate_data(mm, 10, RenderingServer.MULTIMESH_TRANSFORM_3D, false, false, true)

	var command_buffer = RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid(mm)
	print("command buffer: ", command_buffer)
	assert(!command_buffer.is_valid())

	mesh = BoxMesh.new()
	RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh(mm, mesh.get_rid())

	command_buffer = RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid(mm)
	print("command buffer: ", command_buffer)
	assert(command_buffer.is_valid())
```

macOS export: built-in codesign writes non-minimal DER entitlements, app is killed at launch on macOS 26 when three or more entitlements are enabled

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf)

### System information

macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro (arm64), Godot 4.7.2.stable official editor, macOS export with codesign/codesign=1

### Issue description

An app exported with the built-in signer is killed by the kernel at launch (SIGKILL, exit code 137, no output) as soon as the preset enables three or more entitlements. With one or two entitlements, or with none, the same export launches. The same bundle launches after re-signing only the main executable with Apple's codesign using the same entitlements and the hardened runtime, so the bundle contents are fine and the signature Godot writes is what the kernel rejects.

The cause is the DER encoding of the entitlements. PList::save_asn1 picks the number of length octets once, from the size of the whole document, and then every node is written with that many octets. Below 128 bytes every length is in short form and the output is valid DER. At 128 bytes or more every length is written in two-byte long form, including lengths under 128 such as the one-byte booleans. That is legal BER but not DER, which requires the shortest form. Apple's userland tools accept it, which is why codesign --verify --strict reports the app as valid, but the kernel on macOS 26 validates the blob as strict DER and treats the signature as invalid. macOS 15 accepts it (CI runners of another project pass with the same exports).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP, or any project with a macOS preset using the built-in signer.
2. In the preset enable Allow JIT Code Execution, Allow Unsigned Executable Memory and Disable Library Validation (three entitlements).
3. Export, then run Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain from a terminal: it exits with code 137 and prints nothing.
4. Disable one of the three and export again: the app runs and prints plain app started.
5. With the three enabled, re-sign the main executable with Apple's tool and run again: it launches.

codesign -d --entitlements :- --xml Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain > ent.plist
codesign -f -s - --options runtime --entitlements ent.plist Plain.app/Contents/MacOS/Plain

### Tested versions

Also present on current master (0f1b62b7) — same code

### System information

macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro 

### Issue description

On macOS, launching the engine with --embedded outside the editor crashes immediately with signal 11, before anything is rendered. It happens with the default Metal driver and with --rendering-driver opengl3, in a brand new empty project.

The backtrace points repeatedly at mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert (MoltenVK), which is misleading — the crash happens before any shader work; the symbolizer appears to be resolving to the nearest exported symbol.

The cause looks like a null dereference: the DisplayServerMacOSEmbedded constructor in platform/macos/display_server_macos_embedded.mm calls EngineDebugger::get_singleton()->send_message("game_view:set_context_id", ...), and that singleton only exists when the editor launched the process. There are six more unguarded send_message calls in the same file (mouse mode, warp mouse, IME, cursor). OS_MacOS_Embedded::alert() in platform/macos/os_macos.mm already null-checks before the same kind of call.

Crash:
```
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official (ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079)
[1] libsystem_platform.dylib - _sigtramp + 56
[2] mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert(...)
[3] mvk::SPIRVToMSLConverter::convert(...)
````

- On macOS, create a new empty project (one empty scene set as the main scene is enough). Nothing else in it.
- Quit the editor. The project must not be running from it - the crash is about running without the editor attached.
- From a terminal, run the official Godot binary directly on that project with the --embedded flag:
/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --embedded --path /path/to/project --quit-after 120

query:
[Compatibility] Global non-sampler shader uniforms read as 0 when a shader declares 4 or more sampler2D uniforms

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca]
- Not reproducible in: v4.8.dev7 (confirmed regression dev7 -> beta1)

### System information

Godot v4.8.beta1 - macOS 26.6.2 - OpenGL API 4.1 Metal - 90.5 - Compatibility - Apple M2 Max

### Issue description

With the Compatibility renderer, a spatial shader that declares **4 or more `sampler2D` uniforms** reads every **non-sampler global uniform** (`vec4`, `vec2`, `bool`, `uint`, …) with the wrong value. With 0–3 samplers, the same globals read correctly.

- It doesn't matter whether the samplers are `global uniform` or regular material `uniform`, or whether the shader uses them.
- The bad value seems to follow the default texture of the colliding sampler: with `hint_default_black` samplers, globals read as 0; with no hint (white default), they read as 1. That looks like a texture unit/binding collision with the global uniform storage.
- `RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set()` / `global_shader_parameter_set_override()` still work: a shader with fewer than 4 samplers sees the updated values in the same frame.
- No shader compilation errors or warnings are printed.

In a real project this turns the whole scene black in both the editor and the running game, because our main material shader multiplies albedo by global color uniforms and declares about 11 samplers (decals, noise, lookup maps).

**Expected:** global uniform values don't depend on how many samplers a shader declares.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached MRP (Compatibility renderer, one shader global `Test_Color = Vector4(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)`).
2. Run `godot --path <mrp> --script res://repro.gd`.
3. The script renders an unshaded quad with `ALBEDO = Test_Color.rgb`, rebuilding the shader with 0, 3, 4 and 8 extra `uniform sampler2D tex_N : hint_default_black;` declarations, then prints the center pixel each time.

Output on 4.8.beta1:
```
0 samplers -> (0.2471, 0.502, 0.749, 1.0)
3 samplers -> (0.2471, 0.502, 0.749, 1.0)
4 samplers -> (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
8 samplers -> (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
```
Expected: all four lines print the same color.

Shader used (N extra sampler lines):
```glsl
shader_type spatial;
render_mode unshaded;
global uniform vec4 Test_Color;
uniform sampler2D tex_0 : hint_default_black;
uniform sampler2D tex_1 : hint_default_black;
uniform sampler2D tex_2 : hint_default_black;
uniform sampler2D tex_3 : hint_default_black; // adding this 4th one breaks Test_Color
void fragment() { ALBEDO = Test_Color.rgb; }
```

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.beta1 [4d10419ca], official build with the official export templates. The code is unchanged on master [679066724].
- Not reproducible with `binary_format/architecture` set to `arm64`.

### System information

macOS 27.2 (26B118) - Apple Silicon - Godot v4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca]

### Issue description

With a macOS preset's architecture set to `universal` (the default), `--export-release` packages the debug template binaries, and `--export-debug` packages the release ones. The exported app reports the opposite build type.

The source: #124408 added a branch for universal exports to `EditorExportPlatformMacOS::export_project`, and its skip test is inverted:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4d10419cacd6d3009976e8f9fd3abd970fd58018/platform/macos/export/export_plugin.cpp#L2315-L2320

For a release export, `binary_to_use_base` is `godot_macos_release.` ([[L1989](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4d10419cacd6d3009976e8f9fd3abd970fd58018/platform/macos/export/export_plugin.cpp#L1989)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4d10419cacd6d3009976e8f9fd3abd970fd58018/platform/macos/export/export_plugin.cpp#L1989)). So the release binaries are the ones skipped, and the debug `.arm64` and `.x86_64` binaries are merged into the app. Negating the condition (`!file.begins_with(...)`) looks like the fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP, or make a new project whose main scene runs `print("is_debug_build=", OS.is_debug_build())` and then `get_tree().quit()`.
2. Export the "macOS universal" preset with `--export-release`, then run the exported binary from a terminal. It prints `is_debug_build=true`.
3. Export it with `--export-debug` and run it. It prints `is_debug_build=false`.
4. The "macOS arm64" preset prints `false` for release and `true` for debug, as expected.

```
godot --headless --path universal-export-mrp --export-release "macOS universal" out/universal-release.app

```

Trail3D (and mesh_surface_update_index_region) produce no geometry on Web: index buffer is bound to GL_ARRAY_BUFFER

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca]
- The same code is still on master (drivers/gles3/storage/mesh_storage.cpp)

### System information

macOS, Apple M4. Browser: Chromium 152 (Electron), WebGL 2.0 (OpenGL ES 3.0 Chromium), ANGLE Metal renderer. 
Web export with the Compatibility renderer; reproduces with and without thread support.

### Issue description

On the Web export, `Trail3D` nodes render nothing. On desktop they render correctly, including with `--rendering-method gl_compatibility`. The browser console fills with these warnings every frame until WebGL stops reporting them:

```
WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: bindBuffer: element array buffers can not be bound to a different target
WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: bufferSubData: no buffer
WebGL: too many errors, no more errors will be reported to the console for this context.
```

`Trail3D` rebuilds its mesh every frame through `RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_vertex_region`, `mesh_surface_update_attribute_region` and `mesh_surface_update_index_region`. In the GLES3 driver, the index update binds the index buffer to the `GL_ARRAY_BUFFER` target:

```cpp
// drivers/gles3/storage/mesh_storage.cpp, MeshStorage::mesh_surface_update_index_region
glBindBuffer(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, mesh->surfaces[p_surface]->index_buffer);
glBufferSubData(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, p_offset, data_size, r);
glBindBuffer(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, 0);
```

Desktop OpenGL tolerates this. WebGL2 does not allow a buffer first bound as `ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER` to be bound to another target, so the bind fails, `bufferSubData` has no buffer, and the index buffer is never updated. The trail keeps drawing with stale or zeroed indices, which shows up as nothing on screen. This should affect any use of `mesh_surface_update_index_region` on the Web, not only `Trail3D`.

A likely fix is to use the element array target. The VAO is unbound first, because the element array binding is part of VAO state:

```cpp
glBindVertexArray(0);
glBindBuffer(GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, mesh->surfaces[p_surface]->index_buffer);
glBufferSubData(GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, p_offset, data_size, r);
glBindBuffer(GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, 0);
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with the Compatibility renderer.
2. Add a `Camera3D` looking at the origin and a `Trail3D` (default settings) driven by this script:
```gd extends Trail3D
var t := 0.0
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    t += delta
    position = Vector3(cos(t * 2.0), 0.0, sin(t * 2.0)) * 3.0
```
3. Run on desktop: the trail is visible.
4. Export to Web, serve it and open it in a browser: no trail, and the warnings above appear in the console.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached: trail3d-web-mrp.zip. A default Trail3D (lifetime 0.6) moving in a circle, with a small sphere marking its head.
Desktop: the trail follows the sphere. Web (preset included, no thread support, any static server):
the sphere moves, no trail, and the console shows the warnings above.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.dev7 [c971f93e7], 4.8.dev2 [7220d456d], and a custom build of master at 12c17c187 (2026-10-01).
- Not reproducible in: 4.8.dev1 [ebbf577a0], 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf].

#121417 was merged on 2026-07-16, between dev1 (2026-07-06) and dev2 (2026-07-21).

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Unknown (27.0.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (2560x1440 @ 60.00 Hz, 2560x1440 @ 60.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M5 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M5 Pro (18 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The editor crashes on exit when a GDExtension has registered an OpenXR extension wrapper through the deprecated `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` class. An empty project with the Godot OpenXR Vendors add-on (any release up to 4.3.1) is enough; no XR setting needs to be enabled. Expected: clean exit, as in 4.7.2 and 4.8.dev1.

#121417 changed `OpenXRAPI::cleanup_extension_wrappers()` from

```cpp
		if (gdextension_extension_wrapper) {
			memdelete(gdextension_extension_wrapper);
		} else
#endif
		{
			memdelete(extension_wrapper);
		}
```

to

```cpp
		memdelete(gdextension_extension_wrapper);
#endif
		memdelete(extension_wrapper);
```

When the `dynamic_cast` succeeds, both `memdelete` calls now run on the same object, so it is freed twice and the second call crashes in `Object::_predelete()`. The null check added in #121416 does not help here, since the second pointer is dangling rather than null.

The if/else came from #88689, the fix for #88613 (same crash, same add-on). Since #104087 the deprecated class is a plain subclass of `OpenXRExtensionWrapper`, so both pointers are the same address and the `dynamic_cast` no longer serves a purpose.

Reverting the `cleanup_extension_wrappers` hunk of #121417 fixes it: with a local build of master at 12c17c187 the editor crashes on exit as above, and with the hunk reverted it exits cleanly. Deleting the whole `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED` block and keeping a single `memdelete(extension_wrapper)` also fixes it. Happy to open a PR for whichever form is preferred.

The Vendors plugin stopped using the deprecated class in 5.0.0 (GodotVR/godot_openxr_vendors#414), so 5.x releases are not affected. Older releases and any third-party GDExtension still on `OpenXRExtensionWrapperExtension` are.

After a bonkers amount of sniffing through crash reports and testing, I can confirm that the crashes happens when a GC.Collect() takes place while PackedScene.Instantiate() is running (thus the missing indexes from the log in my post above).

As noted, the crash only happens on release builds (and even more frequently on AOT builds), where optimizations tend to affect the lifetime of objects differently.

While I don't have a small repro project, I added a stress test to my game that forced it to quickly loaded packed scenes (that is then instantiated and added to the node tree) for 10 minutes straight. It eventually (often after a few minutes) crashed with the log messages mentioned above. The same thing happens on both 4.7.2 and on 4.8 beta 1.

To get it to crash deterministically, you can force a GC.Collect() from the constructor of the dynamically loaded packed scenes root script:

```csharp
public partial class SceneRoot : Node
{
    public SceneRoot()
    {
        GC.Collect();
        GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
    }
}
```

The "using" workaround suggested by @raulsntos works perfectly, but I landed on this instead since it should work even with other cache methods than IgnoreDeep (where we might not want to call Dispose() on it). Of course, using anyting other than IgnoreDeep assumes the dreaded "Handle is not initialized" bug gets fixed eventually. 

```csharp
var node = packedScene.Instantiate<Node>();
// The use of packedScene here stops the GC from removing it before Instantiate() has finished
GC.KeepAlive(packedScene);
```

While the real fix likely belongs in Godot's generated C# bindings, adding that one GC.KeepAlive() line causes both my deterministic and my 10 min stress test to pass 👍

So that this can eventually be fixed in Godot I installed Claude and had it analyze my source code and try to extract minimal repros of both the packed scene bug and the "Handle is not initialized" bug. A few iterations later it was actually successful 👍
